items.mnemonic: A fire across town can wait. A spark on your own foot can't: you move now.
items.meaning: to be faced with an urgent problem that can't be put off any longer; to be under the gun
items.literal: fire falls on the top of one's foot
items.usage: Usually about a deadline or crisis that has suddenly become pressing, often after putting it off. Neutral to casual; common in speech, essays, and headlines. Frequent frames: 발등에 불이 떨어져야 (only once it's an emergency does one act), and the noun phrase 발등에 떨어진 불 (the most urgent matter): 발등에 떨어진 불부터 끄자.

examples.ko: 평소에는 미루다가 꼭 발등에 불이 떨어져야 움직이는 게 내 문제야.
examples.en: My problem is that I put things off and only get moving when it's an emergency.

examples.ko: 마감이 내일로 다가오자 발등에 불이 떨어진 팀원들이 밤을 새우기 시작했다.
examples.en: With the deadline now tomorrow, the team, suddenly under the gun, started pulling all-nighters.

accepted: be faced with an urgent problem
have an emergency on one's hands

items.mnemonic: The rifle goes on one shoulder only. Whoever shoulders it leads the charge and draws the first shot.
items.meaning: to step up and take on a risky or thankless task on everyone's behalf; to stick one's neck out for the group
items.literal: to shoulder the rifle
items.usage: Workplace, politics, and group settings: someone volunteers (or gets pushed) to raise the complaint, take the blame, or do the dirty work everyone wants done but no one wants to front. Neutral to casual. The verb is 메다 (to shoulder), not 매다 (to tie), a classic spelling slip.

examples.ko: 다들 불만은 많으면서 아무도 총대를 메려고 하지 않았다.
examples.en: Everyone had plenty of complaints, but no one was willing to stick their neck out.

examples.ko: 이번엔 내가 총대 멜게. 대신 다음엔 네 차례야.
examples.en: I'll take this one for the team. But next time it's your turn.

items.mnemonic: Tap the rim and the whole drum hums, without your ever touching the middle.
items.meaning: to hint at something without saying it outright; to talk around the point
items.literal: to strike the rim (of a drum)
items.usage: Describes deliberately oblique talk: instead of hitting the center, you tap the edge and hope the point resonates. Usually critical, and very often as 변죽만 울리다 ('just talking around it'). Common in commentary: 핵심은 피하고 변죽만 울렸다.

examples.ko: 그는 하고 싶은 말이 있는 듯 한참 변죽만 울리다가 결국 돈 얘기를 꺼냈다.
examples.en: He talked around it for ages as if he had something to say, and finally brought up money.

examples.en: Stop dancing around it and get to the point.

items.meaning: a complete transformation for the better; a total makeover

items.usage: A warning, or a rueful realization, about small repeated costs or influences that accumulate: daily coffees, subscriptions, little lies, bad habits. Often shortened to 가랑비에 옷 젖듯, or quoted with -다더니.

items.mnemonic: 바람 = a gust of wind: something sudden knocks your plans over, and the damage is already done.
items.meaning: because of a sudden, unexpected event, with an unwanted result ("…, and so I ended up …")
items.nuance: The cause is typically a sudden or unforeseen event, and its (usually unwanted) result has already happened. The modifier stays -는 even for past events: 넘어지는 바람에 (넘어진 바람에 is nonstandard). The main clause is normally past tense and cannot be a command or suggestion (-(으)세요, -자, -(으)ㅂ시다). The tone is neutral: it reports what happened without blaming anyone or describing the atmosphere.

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 points a finger: the cause is held responsible. -는 바람에 just reports a sudden cause.
-는 통에 blames a hectic, chaotic scene (noise, crowds, commotion); -는 바람에 is typically a single sudden event.

examples.ko: 지하철이 중간에 멈추는 바람에 면접에 20분이나 늦었다.
examples.en: The subway stopped partway, so I ended up a full 20 minutes late for my interview.

examples.ko: 급하게 나오는 바람에 지갑을 집에 두고 왔어요.
examples.en: I left in such a rush that I forgot my wallet at home.

nuance.situation: 밖에 비가 쏟아지기 시작했는데 친구가 막 나가려고 해요. 우산을 가져가라고 말하려면? (It has started pouring and your friend is about to head out. You tell them to take an umbrella.)

options.why: -는 바람에 reports a result that has already happened. It can't lead into a command.
-(으)니까 gives a reason and can be followed by a command or suggestion.
Same problem: -는 통에 explains something that already went wrong, so no command can follow it.

nuance.situation: 지난 금요일 친구 생일 파티에 못 갔어요. 퇴근 직전에 급한 일이 생겼거든요. 사과하면서 이유를 말하려면? (You missed a friend's party last Friday because something urgent came up just before you left work.)

options.why: -느라고 needs the subject's own time-consuming activity (일하느라고 못 갔어). Something that happened to you, like 일이 생기다, can't take it.

options.why: 덕분에 credits a cause for a good result. Missing the party isn't one, so it sounds as if you were glad of the excuse.

items.mnemonic: 탓 = fault, as in "네 탓이야!" The clause is the finger you point at the cause.
items.meaning: because of (a cause blamed for a bad outcome); "owing to", "thanks to" in the sarcastic sense
items.nuance: 탓 means fault or blame, so the clause names a cause held responsible for a negative outcome. Unlike -는 바람에, it takes past (-(으)ㄴ) and adjective forms, and the cause can be a lasting condition rather than a sudden event. It is not used for good outcomes except sarcastically; for those, use 덕분에. Common in both speech and news writing. 탓 also stands alone as a noun: 날씨 탓이다, 남 탓을 하다.

contrasts.note: -는 바람에 neutrally reports a sudden event and only takes -는; -(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 assigns blame and also takes past and adjective forms.
-는 통에 is specifically about commotion; -(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 can blame any cause, including a person or a steady condition.

examples.ko: 평소에 운동을 게을리한 탓에 계단 몇 층만 올라가도 숨이 찬다.

items.mnemonic: Picture yourself stuck in the thick of a noisy crowd: with all that going on, you couldn't do what you meant to.

-(으)ㄹ망정 is a stance-taking, somewhat literary concession: accepting a real hardship on principle, or 'X, but at least Y'. Leading into an offhand practical suggestion like 택시 타자, it sounds stilted; -더라도 or -아/어도 is what people actually say.

items.mnemonic: Same 망정 as in -기에 망정이지 ('good thing that…'): in a bad scenario, find the one thing to hold on to.
items.meaning: (1) even if it means …, (I won't) …; (2) although …, at least …
items.nuance: Two uses, both from the speaker's own standpoint. (1) The speaker accepts a worse outcome rather than do something unacceptable: 굶을망정 남의 돈에는 손대지 않는다. (2) The speaker concedes a drawback and then points to a redeeming fact: 몸은 피곤할망정 마음은 편하다. Either way the main clause is the speaker's stance or assessment; it rarely leads into an everyday request. It is a near-synonym of -(으)ㄹ지언정, which sounds more emphatic and bookish.

contrasts.note: Near-synonyms in both uses; -(으)ㄹ지언정 sounds more emphatic and bookish.
-더라도 is a neutral 'even if' and can lead into advice, commands, and suggestions.
-느니 (차라리) marks the option rejected; -(으)ㄹ망정 marks the hardship accepted: 굶을망정 구걸은 안 한다 ≈ 구걸하느니 차라리 굶겠다.

items.meaning: even if …, (I will) never …; would sooner … than …
items.nuance: An emphatic, somewhat literary concession: the speaker accepts the first (bad) scenario and flatly rules out the second. The main clause is typically a refusal or negation (-지 않겠다, 못 하다, -(으)ㄹ 수 없다), often reinforced by 차라리 in the first clause. Like -(으)ㄹ망정, it can also concede a past fact before a redeeming point (졌을지언정 정신력만큼은 뒤지지 않았다). At home in speeches, op-eds, and dramatic declarations.

contrasts.note: Near-synonym in both uses; -(으)ㄹ망정 is a little less emphatic and more conversational.
The same choice seen from the other side: -느니 attaches to the option rejected, -(으)ㄹ지언정 to the hardship accepted.

-(으)ㄹ지언정 sets up a hardship the speaker accepts while ruling something out. Its main clause is a refusal or negation, not a request.

items.mnemonic: 커녕 slams the door on the expectation: 'Praise? Far from it.'
items.meaning: far from …; let alone … (the expected thing didn't happen, and often the opposite did)
items.nuance: Emphatically denies the first, expected or hoped-for situation. The second clause either goes further in the same negative direction, often with 도/조차 + a negative (인사는커녕 쳐다보지도 않았다), or reports the opposite, often with 오히려/도리어 (칭찬하기는커녕 오히려 화를 냈다). Common in speech and writing, and frequently tinged with indignation.

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄴ/는 데다가 adds a fact that did happen; -기는커녕 denies the first fact outright.
Same contrast: -(으)ㄹ뿐더러 affirms both points.

nuance.situation: 퇴근길에 친구가 좋아하는 빵이 보여서 하나 사 왔어요. 친구에게 건네면서 하는 말은? (On your way home you spotted a pastry your friend loves and bought one. You hand it over.)

options.text: 네가 좋아하는 빵이 보이길래 하나 사 왔어.
options.why: -길래: you came across something, and the main clause is what you did in response.

options.text: 네가 좋아하는 빵이 보이길래 하나 사 와.
options.why: -길래 can't lead into a command; its main clause reports what was done in response.

options.text: 네가 좋아하는 빵이 보이는 통에 하나 사 왔어.
options.why: -는 통에 blames a commotion for an unwanted result. Spotting a pastry is neither.

items.mnemonic: -(으)니 'since' + 만큼 'to that degree': since it matters this much, act to match.
items.meaning: since / given that … (so it is only fitting that …)
items.nuance: States a premise from which the main clause follows as the fitting response or natural judgment: 'given that X, (naturally) Y'. Formal; common in speeches, notices, and editorials. Unlike -기에 and -길래, the main clause can be a request, command, or suggestion (중요한 회의이니만큼 늦지 마세요). Close to the 'since' sense of -(으)ㄴ/는 만큼.

contrasts.note: -기에 also gives formal grounds but can't lead into a request or command.
-길래 is colloquial and can't lead into a request either.

examples.ko: 이번 결정은 회사의 미래가 걸린 문제이니만큼 신중하게 검토해야 한다.
examples.en: Since the company's future hinges on this decision, it has to be reviewed carefully.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 모이는 자리니만큼 다들 시간 맞춰 와 주세요.
examples.en: Since it's been a while since we all got together, please be on time.

Fine in everyday speech; the cue asks for the more formal -(으)니만큼.

nuance.situation: 팀원들에게 중요한 발표가 있으니 조금 일찍 와 달라고 공지하려고 해요. (A note asking the team to come early because there's a key presentation.)

options.text: 중요한 발표가 있는 날이니만큼 조금 일찍 와 주세요.
options.why: -(으)니만큼 sets up a premise and can lead into a request.

options.text: 중요한 발표가 있는 날이기에 조금 일찍 와 주세요.
options.why: -기에 can't be followed by a request or command.

options.text: 중요한 발표가 있는 날이길래 조금 일찍 와 주세요.
options.why: -길래 can't be followed by a request either, and it implies you just happened to notice the fact.

nuance.situation: 장마철이라 외출할 때 우산을 꼭 챙기라는 안내문을 쓰려고 해요. (A notice reminding residents to take umbrellas during the monsoon season.)

options.text: 장마철이니만큼 외출하실 때는 우산을 꼭 챙기십시오.
options.why: -(으)니만큼 sets up a premise and can lead into a request.

options.text: 장마철이길래 외출하실 때는 우산을 꼭 챙기십시오.
options.why: -길래 can't lead into a request, and it frames the season as something you just happened to notice.

items.mnemonic: 셈 = counting (셈하다): do the math, and this is what it comes to.
items.meaning: it amounts to …; in effect …; you could say …
items.nuance: A conclusion reached by reckoning from the facts: add things up, or look at them a certain way, and this is what it comes to. Often with 결국, 사실상, or 거의. Related set phrases: 셈 치다 ('treat it as', 기부한 셈 치자) and 셈이 되다.

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄴ/는 격이다 likens the situation to a typical, often proverbial scenario; -(으)ㄴ/는 셈이다 reckons from the facts.
-(으)ㄴ/는 거나 마찬가지다 asserts equivalence more bluntly and colloquially ('as good as').

examples.ko: 한 달에 이틀밖에 못 쉬었으니 사실상 매일 출근한 셈이다.
examples.en: I only had two days off all month, so in effect I went to work every day.

examples.ko: 할인 쿠폰까지 쓰면 반값에 산 셈이에요.
examples.en: With the coupon on top, you've basically bought it at half price.

nearMiss.hint: The results are already in: use the past form, 붙은 셈이다.

nearMiss.hint: 쉽다 is ㅂ-irregular: 쉬운 셈이다.

nearMiss.hint: 요즘 describes an ongoing state: 일하는 셈이다.

cloze.sentence: 강의를 반도 안 들었으니 사실상 안 {{}}.

nearMiss.hint: 낫다 is ㅅ-irregular: 나은 셈이다.

cloze.sentence: "그럼 결국 둘이 헤어진 거야?" "뭐, {{}}."
cloze.en: "So they broke up in the end?" "Well, more or less."

nearMiss.hint: 그렇다 is ㅎ-irregular: 그런 셈이야.

nuance.situation: 월세 팔십만 원에 관리비가 이십만 원이에요. 실제로 매달 얼마를 내는지 정리해서 말하려고 해요. (Rent plus building fees: you sum up what you actually pay each month.)

options.text: 결국 한 달에 백만 원을 내는 셈이야.
options.why: -는 셈이다 states the result of a reckoning: add it up and that's what it comes to.

options.text: 결국 한 달에 백만 원을 내기 십상이야.
options.why: -기 십상이다 warns that something bad is likely; it doesn't state a computed total.

options.text: 결국 한 달에 백만 원을 내기 마련이야.
options.why: -기 마련이다 states a general truth about how things tend to go, not the result of this calculation.

nuance.situation: 친구에게 빌려준 돈을 돌려받기는 틀린 것 같아요. 그냥 기부한 것으로 여기고 잊기로 했어요. (You'll never see the money you lent a friend again, so you decide to write it off as a donation.)

options.why: 셈 치다 is the set frame for "treat it as": count it as a donation.
격 has no "treat it as" use; that frame belongs to 셈 (셈 치다).

items.mnemonic: 格 = pattern: the situation fits a familiar pattern, usually one from a proverb.
items.meaning: it's like …; it's a case of … (likening the situation to a stock, often proverbial scenario)
items.nuance: Compares the present situation to a stock scenario, very often a proverb or idiom: 소 잃고 외양간 고치는 격이다, 계란으로 바위 치는 격이다, 제 발등을 찍은 격이다. The tone is usually critical or ironic; frequent in editorials and commentary. 격 (格) here means 'pattern, kind'.

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄴ/는 셈이다 reckons from the facts; -(으)ㄴ/는 격이다 holds up a figurative mirror.
A blunter, more colloquial claim of equivalence.

examples.ko: 사고가 난 뒤에야 안전 점검을 하겠다니, 소 잃고 외양간 고치는 격이다.
examples.en: Promising safety checks only after the accident: that's locking the barn after the horse has bolted.

examples.ko: 자기가 만든 규정 때문에 자기가 승진을 못 했으니, 제 발등을 제가 찍은 격이지.
examples.en: He couldn't get promoted because of a rule he wrote himself. He shot himself in the foot.

cloze.sentence: 거대 기업을 상대로 혼자 소송을 걸겠다니, 계란으로 바위 {{}}.
cloze.en: Suing a giant corporation all on your own? That's like throwing an egg at a rock.

nearMiss.hint: With a proverb as the comparison, the standard fit is -는 격이다; the cue asks for it.

cloze.en: Our team lead delivered, and now we're getting praised too. Talk about riding someone else's coattails.

nearMiss.hint: 불다 drops its ㄹ before -는: 부는 격이다.

cloze.en: Rushing to make excuses when nobody even asked? That's a guilty conscience giving itself away.

cloze.en: I hate client dinners, but I can't skip them. It's like eating mustard through tears.

nearMiss.hint: With a proverb as the comparison, the standard fit is -는 격이다; the cue asks for it.

cloze.sentence: 환불받으러 갔다가 추가 요금까지 냈으니, 혹 떼러 갔다가 혹 붙여 {{}}.
cloze.en: I went for a refund and ended up paying an extra fee: went to get a lump removed and came back with another.

nearMiss.hint: It has already happened: 온 격이다.

cloze.sentence: 타결을 눈앞에 두고 막말로 협상을 깨다니, 다 된 밥에 재를 {{}}.
cloze.en: Wrecking the talks with a careless remark just before a deal: that's throwing ashes on a perfectly cooked pot of rice.

nearMiss.hint: The talks have already collapsed: 뿌린 격이다.

nuance.situation: 작은 스타트업이 대기업과 정면 승부를 하겠다고 해요. 무모해 보이는 상황을 속담에 빗대어 말하려면? (A tiny startup plans to take on a conglomerate head-on. You liken it to a proverb.)

options.why: -는 격이다 likens the situation to a stock scenario, here the egg and the rock.
-(으)ㄴ 탓이다 blames a cause for a bad result that already happened; nothing has happened yet.
-기 마련이다 states a general tendency; it can't hold up a proverb as a comparison.

nuance.situation: 새로 들어온 경력직이 오래 일한 직원을 밀어내고 그 자리를 차지했어요. 속담 '굴러온 돌이 박힌 돌 뺀다'에 빗대려면? (An experienced new hire pushed out a long-serving employee and took her place. You liken it to the proverb about the rolling stone dislodging the embedded one.)

options.text: 굴러온 돌이 박힌 돌 빼낸 격이네.
options.why: -(으)ㄴ 격이다 likens what has happened to the proverb's scenario, with the past modifier -(으)ㄴ.

options.text: 굴러온 돌이 박힌 돌 빼냈는 격이네.
options.why: The modifier before 격 is -(으)ㄴ for a past event (빼낸); *빼냈는 isn't a form.

options.text: 굴러온 돌이 박힌 돌 빼낼 지경이네.
options.why: -(으)ㄹ 지경이다 says things have nearly reached an extreme state. It doesn't liken anything to a proverb, and the ousting has already happened.

items.mnemonic: 거나 = 것이나 'it may as well be': two things side by side, with no difference worth mentioning.
items.meaning: is as good as …; is no different from …
items.nuance: Asserts that one thing is, for practical purposes, the same as another: 'it's as good as …'. Colloquial in tone (거나 is short for 것이나) and often emphatic or slightly exaggerated: 도장만 안 찍었지 다 된 거나 마찬가지야. With nouns: N(이)나 마찬가지다. A common variant ends in 다름없다: -(으)ㄴ 거나 다름없다.

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄴ/는 셈이다 is a more measured reckoning, at home in writing.
-(으)ㄴ/는 격이다 compares with a figurative scenario rather than asserting equivalence.

examples.ko: 결승골이 들어간 순간 우승한 거나 마찬가지였다.
examples.en: The moment the winning goal went in, the title was as good as won.

examples.ko: 그 선배는 나한테 친언니나 마찬가지야.
examples.en: She's like a real big sister to me.

cloze.sentence: 계약서에 도장만 안 찍었지 사실상 다 {{}}.
cloze.en: We haven't stamped the contract yet, but it's as good as done.

nearMiss.hint: Close in meaning; the cue asks for -(으)ㄴ 거나 마찬가지다.

cloze.sentence: 하루 종일 휴대폰만 봤으면 {{}}.
cloze.en: If you spent the whole day on your phone, you might as well have been goofing off.

nearMiss.hint: 놀다 drops its ㄹ before -ㄴ: 논 거나 마찬가지야.

cloze.en: Selling that stock now is as good as locking in the loss.

nearMiss.hint: Close in meaning; the cue asks for -는 거나 마찬가지다.

cloze.sentence: 직함만 없지 사실상 그 사람이 {{}}.
cloze.en: He doesn't have the title, but he's practically the team lead.

nearMiss.hint: 팀장 ends in a consonant, so it takes 이나: 팀장이나 마찬가지야.

cloze.en: If you read the summary carefully, it's as good as having heard the whole lecture.

nearMiss.hint: 듣다 is ㄷ-irregular: 들은 거나 마찬가지야.

cloze.sentence: 10년을 같이 산 고양이는 나한테 {{}}.
cloze.en: The cat I've lived with for ten years is like my own child.

nuance.situation: 어릴 때부터 같이 자란 이웃 언니를 소개하면서 가족이나 다름없다는 뜻을 전하려고 해요. (Introducing a neighbor you grew up with, you say she's practically family.)

options.why: N(이)나 마찬가지다 asserts practical equivalence: she's as good as family.
-(으)ㄴ 격이다 likens a situation to a stock scenario; it can't say a person is like family, and the stacked modifier doesn't work.
-기 마련이다 states a general tendency; 'bound to be family' makes no sense here.

nuance.situation: 동료가 사직서는 아직 안 냈지만, 이직할 회사도 정해졌고 인수인계도 하고 있어요. (A coworker hasn't handed in his notice yet, but he's lined up a new job and is already handing over his work.)

options.text: 말만 안 했지 그만둔 거나 마찬가지야.
options.why: -(으)ㄴ 거나 마찬가지다: for practical purposes, he has already quit.
-기 마련이다 states a general tendency; it can't say that this person has effectively quit.
-(으)ㄴ 탓이다 blames a cause for a bad outcome; nothing here is being blamed.

items.mnemonic: 마련 = arrangement (as in 마련하다): it's all been arranged in advance. That's simply how things go.
items.meaning: is bound to …; naturally / inevitably …
items.nuance: States what naturally or inevitably happens as a general rule, not what happened in one case. contrasts.note: -는 법이다 sounds more aphoristic, like a rule of life or a lesson, and is often admonishing.
-기 십상이다 predicts that something (bad) is likely in a specific situation, often as a warning.

items.nuance: Predicts that, under the stated condition, an almost always undesirable result is very likely. Typically follows a conditional or warning frame: -다가는/-(으)면 … -기 십상이다. From 십상팔구 (十常八九, 'eight or nine times out of ten'). Attached to a good outcome it sounds off, even sarcastic; for those, -기 마련이다 or plain -(으)ㄹ 것이다 fits.

contrasts.note: -기 마련이다 states a general truth, good or bad; -기 십상이다 warns of a likely bad result in a particular situation.
-(으)ㄹ세라 describes the precaution someone takes against such a feared outcome.

items.mnemonic: 나머지 = the remainder: so much feeling that the overflow spills into an action.

items.mnemonic: 못해 = 'couldn't (go on)': you tried to keep going, and you couldn't.
items.meaning: (V) unable to keep … up any longer, finally …; (A) so … that it goes beyond into …
items.nuance: Two uses. With verbs of enduring or watching (참다, 견디다, 보다, 기다리다), the person held out as long as they could and then acted: 보다못해 한마디 했다 ('unable to stand by any longer'). With adjectives, a quality is pushed past its limit into a further, more extreme state: 하얗다 못해 창백하다, 지루하다 못해 졸리다. 참다못해 and 보다못해 are adverbs in 표준국어대사전 and are written closed up; elsewhere keep the space (기다리다 못해, 지루하다 못해).

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄴ 나머지 is an excess of feeling causing an (unintended) action; -다 못해 is a limit of endurance reached.
-(으)ㄹ 지경이다 is the verge of an extreme; -다 못해 has already crossed into it.

nuance.situation: 공사 소음이 몇 주째 이어지자 결국 관리실에 항의 전화를 했어요. (After weeks of construction noise, you finally called the building office to complain.)

options.why: -다 못해 with 참다: you held out as long as you could, then acted.
-(으)ㄴ 나머지 needs an excess of feeling (화가 난 나머지 would work); 'having endured' isn't such a state.
-는 바람에 makes enduring the sudden cause of an unwanted result, which turns the logic upside down.

nuance.situation: 환자의 얼굴에 핏기가 하나도 없었어요. 하얀 정도를 넘어 아파 보였다고 쓰려면? (The patient's face had no color at all: beyond pale, it looked sickly.)

options.why: A-다 못해 pushes a quality past its limit into a more extreme state on the same scale.
Rosy cheeks go the other way. -다 못해 needs a more extreme degree of the same quality.

items.meaning: (1) as (you know / can see / heard); (2) in -다시피 하다, practically, all but
items.nuance: (1) With verbs of knowing and perceiving only (알다, 보다, 듣다, 말하다, 느끼다): 'as you know/see/heard', pointing to shared knowledge. Very common in presentations and announcements (보시다시피, 아시다시피, 말씀드렸다시피). (2) In -다시피 하다: doing something so much or so nearly that it practically amounts to it: 굶다시피 하다 ('all but starve'), 살다시피 하다 ('practically live somewhere'), 뛰다시피 걷다 ('half-run').

contrasts.note: -듯이 makes a simile ('like, as if'); -다시피 points to shared knowledge or means 'practically'.

items.mnemonic: 듯 = semblance: it looks just like…
items.meaning: like, as if; just as
items.nuance: Two structures. Attached directly to a stem, -듯(이) draws a comparison of manner, often in set similes: 물 쓰듯 돈을 쓰다 ('spend money like water'), 밥 먹듯이 거짓말을 하다 ('lie as easily as eating'), 비 오듯 땀을 흘리다. After a modifier (-(으)ㄴ/는 듯이) or a quotation (-다는 듯이) it means 'as if', often about appearances: 아무 일도 없었다는 듯이 웃었다. The 이 is optional in both.

contrasts.note: -다시피 never means 'as if'; it points to shared knowledge or means 'practically'.
-(으)ㄴ/는 양 also means 'as if' but often suggests a false or presumptuous pose, and it's more literary.

items.mnemonic: 양 (樣) = appearance: all appearance, no substance.
items.meaning: as if, pretending that (often a false or presumptuous pose)
items.nuance: Literary and written. Describes someone acting as if something were so, usually implying that it isn't, or that the pose is presumptuous: 자기가 사장이라도 된 양 지시를 내렸다. With 하다 it means 'to pretend' (모르는 양하다). It is mostly about people's poses and attitudes; literary prose can extend it to things (꽃잎이 춤추는 양 흩날렸다), but for an everyday 'looks like (rain)', -(으)ㄹ 듯하다 or -(으)ㄴ 것 같다 is the natural choice. (A separate pattern, -(으)ㄹ 양으로, means 'intending to'.)

contrasts.note: -듯이 is the neutral 'as if, like'; -(으)ㄴ/는 양 adds a hint that the pose is false or presumptuous.

contrasts.note: -다시피 하다 is 'practically did (it fully)'; -는 둥 마는 둥 is 'barely did it'.

items.mnemonic: -느니 points at the option you're throwing out; 차라리 picks up the one you'll grudgingly keep.
items.meaning: rather than …, (I'd) sooner …
items.nuance: Both options are bad; the speaker rejects the one marked with -느니 and picks the other as the lesser evil. Verbs only (plus 있다/없다). The main clause typically ends in -는 게 낫다, -겠다, or a suggestion, and 차라리 or 아예 often reinforces it. Common in speech and writing alike.

contrasts.note: The same choice from the other side: -(으)ㄹ지언정 marks the hardship accepted, -느니 the option rejected.
-(으)ㄹ망정 also marks the hardship accepted: 굶을망정 구걸은 안 한다 ≈ 구걸하느니 차라리 굶겠다.

examples.en: We handled it without going through proper procedures, and it became a problem later.

cloze.sentence: 법안은 상임위원회 심사를 {{}} 본회의에 상정되었다.
cloze.en: After standing committee review, the bill was put before the plenary session.

cloze.sentence: 수많은 시행착오를 {{}} 지금의 방식이 자리를 잡았다.
cloze.en: The current method only took hold after a great deal of trial and error.

nuance.situation: 신입 사원은 3개월의 수습 기간을 마쳐야 정식 직원이 된다. (New hires become permanent after a three-month probation.)

options.text: 3개월의 수습 기간을 거쳐 정식 직원이 된다.
options.why: A set stage or procedure you pass through is 거치다.

options.text: 3개월의 수습 기간을 겪어 정식 직원이 된다.
options.why: 겪다 is for something that happens to you, usually hardship or change (어려움을 겪다). A fixed stage is 거치다.

options.text: 3개월의 수습 기간을 지나쳐 정식 직원이 된다.
options.why: 지나치다 means to go past without stopping, or to overdo something.

collocations.en: to pull up at the door

examples.ko: 건물 앞은 주차 금지라서 뒤쪽 골목에 차를 댔어요.
examples.en: There's no parking in front of the building, so I parked in the alley out back.

examples.ko: 기사님, 저기 편의점 앞에 대 주세요.
examples.en: Driver, could you pull up in front of that convenience store?

cloze.sentence: 비가 오니까 현관 바로 앞에 차를 {{}} 줄게.
cloze.en: It's raining, so I'll pull the car right up to the entrance for you.

cloze.sentence: 주차장이 꽉 차서 차를 어디에 {{}} 할지 모르겠어요.
cloze.en: The lot is full, so I don't know where I'm supposed to park.

examples.ko: 그는 몸이 안 좋다는 핑계를 대고 회식에 빠졌다.
examples.en: He used feeling unwell as an excuse to skip the staff dinner.

examples.ko: 늦은 이유를 대 봐. 납득이 가면 넘어갈게.
examples.en: Go on, tell me why you're late. If it makes sense, I'll let it go.

cloze.sentence: 숙제를 안 해 온 학생들은 저마다 그럴듯한 핑계를 {{}} 바빴다.
cloze.en: The students who hadn't done their homework were all busy coming up with plausible excuses.

cloze.sentence: 근거를 {{}} 못하면 그 주장은 받아들일 수 없어요.
cloze.en: If you can't give any grounds, that claim can't be accepted.

nuance.situation: 늦잠을 자 놓고 버스가 안 와서 늦었다고 했다. (You overslept but blamed the bus.)

options.why: Making an excuse is 핑계를 대다.
들다 takes 예 or 이유 (예를 들다, 이유를 들어 거절하다). With 핑계 the verb is 대다; 핑계를 들다 sounds off.

collocations.en: to lift noodles out (of the water)
to fish out the solids and eat them
to pull a drowning person out

examples.ko: 면이 다 익으면 체로 건져서 찬물에 헹궈 주세요.
examples.en: When the noodles are done, lift them out with a strainer and rinse them in cold water.

examples.ko: 강에 떨어뜨린 휴대폰을 낚시꾼이 그물로 건져 줬다.
examples.en: A fisherman fished out the phone I'd dropped in the river with his net.

cloze.sentence: 국물은 남기고 건더기만 {{}} 먹었다.
cloze.en: I left the broth and fished out just the solids to eat.

nuance.situation: 끓는 냄비에서 삶은 달걀을 국자로 꺼냈다. (You lifted the boiled eggs out of the pot with a ladle.)

options.why: Lifting something solid out of liquid is 건지다.
건네다 means to hand something over to someone.
거르다 means to strain or filter a liquid (or to skip a meal). Lifting solids out one by one is 건지다.

collocations.en: to break even; to get one's money back
to get one good photo out of it

examples.ko: 여행 내내 비만 왔지만 그래도 마음에 드는 사진 몇 장은 건졌어.
examples.en: It rained the whole trip, but I still got a few photos I like out of it.

examples.ko: 사고 차량은 크게 부서졌지만 운전자는 기적적으로 목숨을 건졌다.
examples.en: The car was badly wrecked, but the driver miraculously escaped with his life.

cloze.sentence: 주식으로 손해만 보다가 겨우 본전을 {{}} 바로 다 팔았다.
cloze.en: After nothing but losses on stocks, I finally got back to break-even and sold everything right away.

cloze.sentence: 세 시간짜리 세미나였는데 솔직히 {{}} 게 하나도 없었어.
cloze.en: It was a three-hour seminar, and honestly I didn't get a single thing out of it.

nuance.situation: 투자금을 다 잃을 뻔했는데 겨우 원금만은 되찾았다. (You nearly lost everything but got your principal back.)

options.why: Salvaging something from a loss is 건지다 (본전을 건지다).
견디다 means to endure or hold out. It doesn't mean getting money back.
거르다 means to strain or filter, or to skip (a meal).

meanings: to wear (on the fingers or hands)
to put on (a ring, gloves, lenses)

collocations.en: to fold one's arms; to link arms

examples.ko: 결혼반지를 끼고 설거지하다가 하수구에 빠뜨릴 뻔했어.
examples.en: I was doing the dishes with my wedding ring on and nearly lost it down the drain.

examples.ko: 그는 팔짱을 낀 채 아무 말 없이 회의 내용을 듣고만 있었다.
examples.en: He sat with his arms folded, just listening to the meeting without a word.

cloze.sentence: 손이 시려서 장갑을 두 겹이나 {{}} 나왔다.
cloze.en: My hands were freezing, so I came out wearing two pairs of gloves.

cloze.sentence: 눈이 너무 건조해서 렌즈를 {{}} 수가 없어.
cloze.en: My eyes are so dry I can't put my contacts in.

nuance.situation: 추운 날 손을 보호하려고 장갑을 착용했다. (You put on gloves on a cold day.)

options.why: Things you slip your fingers or hands into take 끼다.
쓰다 is for things on the head or face: hats, glasses, masks.
차다 is for things strapped or hung on: a watch, a belt.

examples.ko: 새벽에 안개가 짙게 끼어서 고속도로에서 사고가 잇따랐다.
examples.en: Thick fog set in before dawn, and there was a string of accidents on the expressway.

examples.ko: 오래 안 쓴 키보드라 자판 사이에 먼지가 잔뜩 꼈네.
examples.en: This keyboard hasn't been used in ages. There's dust packed between all the keys.

cloze.sentence: 하늘에 구름이 잔뜩 {{}} 있어서 별이 하나도 안 보였다.
cloze.en: The sky was so overcast that not a single star was visible.

cloze.sentence: 물때가 {{}} 욕실 타일을 주말에 박박 닦았다.
cloze.en: Over the weekend I gave the bathroom tiles, crusted with soap scum, a hard scrub.

nuance.situation: 아침 일찍 창밖을 보니 온 동네가 뿌옇게 보였다. (Early morning: the whole neighborhood looks hazy.)

options.why: Fog, cloud, dust and grime take 끼다: they form and settle over something.
묻다 is for a liquid or powder getting on something (옷에 잉크가 묻다). Fog doesn't 묻다.

examples.ko: 십 년 넘게 준비한 끝에 그녀는 마침내 자기 책을 내겠다는 꿈을 이뤘다.
examples.en: After more than ten years of preparation, she finally realized her dream of publishing her own book.

examples.ko: 양측은 밤샘 협상 끝에 극적으로 합의를 이루었다.
examples.en: After all-night negotiations, the two sides dramatically reached an agreement.

cloze.sentence: 올해 세운 목표를 다 {{}} 못했지만 절반은 해냈다.
cloze.en: I didn't achieve every goal I set this year, but I got halfway.

cloze.sentence: 작은 목표라도 하나씩 {{}} 가다 보면 자신감이 붙는다.
cloze.en: If you keep achieving goals one at a time, however small, your confidence builds.

nuance.situation: 오랜 노력 끝에 바라던 것을 손에 넣었다. (After long effort, you got what you'd hoped for.)

options.why: Achieving a dream or goal is 이루다, with an object.
이르다 (이르러, 이르렀다) means to reach a point and takes 에: 결론에 이르다.
거두다 goes with results and wins (성과를 거두다, 승리를 거두다), not dreams.

examples.ko: 붉은 단풍이 파란 하늘과 선명한 대조를 이루었다.
examples.en: The red autumn leaves stood out vividly against the blue sky.

examples.ko: 새 휴대폰 출시일에 매장 앞은 아침부터 장사진을 이뤘다.
examples.en: On the new phone's launch day, a long line formed outside the store from early morning.

cloze.sentence: 이 도시는 오래된 한옥과 현대식 건물이 묘한 조화를 {{}} 있다.
cloze.en: In this city, old hanok and modern buildings sit together in a curious harmony.

cloze.sentence: 그 시절 문단의 주류를 {{}} 것은 참여 문학이었다.
cloze.en: What made up the literary mainstream in those days was socially engaged literature.

items.mnemonic: 빌다 (wish, beg) → 빌어, 빕니다. 빌리다 (borrow) → 빌려. The extra 리 is what you borrow.

collocations.en: to pray for the soul of the departed

examples.ko: 새해 첫날 해돋이를 보면서 가족들 건강을 빌었어요.
examples.en: On New Year's Day, watching the sunrise, I prayed for my family's health.

examples.ko: 면접 잘 보고 와. 행운을 빌게!
examples.en: Good luck at the interview. I'll keep my fingers crossed!

examples.ko: 고인의 명복을 빕니다.
examples.en: May the departed rest in peace.

cloze.sentence: 합격 발표 날, 어머니는 아침부터 두 손을 모으고 {{}} 계셨다.
cloze.en: On the day the results came out, my mother sat with her hands clasped in prayer from the morning on.

cloze.sentence: 다들 시험 잘 보길 {{}}.
cloze.en: I hope you all do well on the exam.

nearMiss.hint: Check the spelling: -(으)ㄹ게 is written with ㄱ.

nuance.situation: 친구의 앞날에 행운이 있기를 바란다. (You wish your friend luck.)

options.why: Wishing or praying is 빌다 → 빌어.
빌려 comes from 빌리다 (borrow). Wishing is 빌다 → 빌어.
-(으)러 means "in order to" and needs a verb of motion after it (빌러 가다).

examples.ko: 약속을 또 어겨서 여자 친구한테 싹싹 빌었어.
examples.en: I broke my promise again, so I groveled to my girlfriend.

examples.ko: 그는 피해자 가족 앞에 무릎을 꿇고 용서를 빌었다.
examples.en: He knelt before the victim's family and begged their forgiveness.

cloze.sentence: 이제 와서 잘못했다고 {{}} 봐야 이미 늦었어.
cloze.en: There's no point begging forgiveness now. It's too late.

nearMiss.hint: 빌려 is from 빌리다 (borrow); begging is a different verb.

cloze.sentence: 아이는 다시는 안 그러겠다며 엄마에게 {{}}.
cloze.en: The child begged his mother's forgiveness, promising never to do it again.

collocations.en: (I'd like to) take this opportunity to

examples.ko: 이 자리를 빌려 그동안 도와주신 모든 분께 감사드립니다.
examples.en: I'd like to take this opportunity to thank everyone who has helped along the way.

examples.ko: 한 평론가의 말을 빌리자면, 이 소설은 '실패한 걸작'이다.
examples.en: To borrow one critic's words, this novel is a "failed masterpiece."

examples.ko: 평소엔 말도 못 붙이더니 술기운을 빌려 고백을 했다.
examples.en: He'd never even managed to talk to her, but with a little Dutch courage he confessed.

cloze.sentence: 작가는 수상 소감에서 이 자리를 {{}} 번역가에게 고마움을 전했다.
cloze.en: In her acceptance speech, the author took the opportunity to thank her translator.

cloze.sentence: 어느 시인의 표현을 {{}} 그 시절 우리는 '눈부시게 가난했다.'
cloze.en: To borrow a poet's phrase, in those days we were "dazzlingly poor."

items.mnemonic: Granting a request is the single word 들어주다. "Listen to (someone)" is 듣다 + -어 주다 and is spaced in careful writing: 얘기를 들어 주다.

collocations.en: to give in to a demand

examples.ko: 웬만한 부탁은 다 들어주는데 돈 빌려 달라는 건 좀 곤란해.
examples.en: I'll do you most favors, but lending money is a bit much.

examples.ko: 회사는 결국 노조의 요구를 일부 들어주기로 했다.
examples.en: The company finally agreed to meet some of the union's demands.

cloze.sentence: 아이가 하도 졸라서 강아지를 키우고 싶다는 소원을 {{}} 수밖에 없었다.
cloze.en: My kid begged so much that I had no choice but to grant her wish for a puppy.

cloze.sentence: 그렇게 무리한 요구를 다 {{}} 계약할 이유는 없다.
cloze.en: There's no reason to sign if it means giving in to such unreasonable demands.

nuance.situation: 친구가 이삿짐 나르는 걸 도와 달라고 해서 도와주기로 했다. (A friend asked for help moving, and you agreed.)

options.why: Granting a request is 들어주다, written as one word.
들려주다 means to tell or play something so someone hears it (이야기를 들려주다).
들어 보다 is just hearing the request out. It doesn't say you agreed.

examples.ko: 예약 없이 찾아온 손님들을 그냥 돌려보낼 수밖에 없었다.
examples.en: We had no choice but to turn away the guests who showed up without a reservation.

examples.ko: 멀리서 왔는데 빈손으로 돌려보내기가 미안해서 차라도 한잔 대접했어요.
examples.en: They'd come a long way and I felt bad sending them off empty-handed, so I at least offered them some tea.

cloze.sentence: 주문한 것과 다른 색이 와서 상품을 판매자에게 {{}} 했다.
cloze.en: The wrong color arrived, so I had to send the item back to the seller.

cloze.sentence: 서류 하나 빠졌다고 민원인을 그냥 {{}} 건 너무하잖아요.
cloze.en: Sending someone away just because one document was missing is a bit much.

nuance.situation: 청탁성 선물이 배달되자 그는 뜯지도 않고 보낸 사람에게 다시 보냈다. (A gift that came with strings attached arrived; he sent it back unopened.)

options.why: Sending something or someone back where it came from is 돌려보내다.
내보내다 means to send or let out of a space, to dismiss, or to broadcast. It doesn't mean returning to the sender.
되돌아가다 is intransitive (go back). It can't take 선물을 as an object.

collocations.en: to put one's house on the market
to bring out a new product

examples.ko: 이사 가려고 지난달에 집을 내놨는데 아직 보러 오는 사람이 없네.
examples.en: We put the house on the market last month to move, but nobody's come to see it yet.

examples.ko: 업체는 기존 모델보다 가격을 낮춘 보급형 제품을 내놓았다.
examples.en: The company brought out a budget model priced below its existing line.

cloze.sentence: 오래 몰던 차를 중고 시장에 {{}} 일주일 만에 팔렸다.
cloze.en: I put the car I'd driven for years on the used market, and it sold within a week.

cloze.sentence: 그 출판사는 해마다 번역 시리즈를 꾸준히 {{}} 있다.
cloze.en: That publisher has been steadily bringing out a translation series every year.

nuance.situation: 회사가 새 스마트폰 모델을 출시했다. (A company launched a new smartphone model.)

options.why: Bringing a product out onto the market is 내놓다.
꺼내다 means to take something out of a container, or to bring up a topic.
내보내다 means to send people or things out of a place, or to air a broadcast.

meanings: to come up with (measures, a plan)

collocations.en: to issue a statement of position

examples.ko: 정부는 전세 사기 피해자를 위한 지원책을 내놓았다.
examples.en: The government put forward support measures for victims of jeonse fraud.

examples.ko: 회의는 세 시간이나 했는데 아무도 뾰족한 수를 못 내놓더라.
examples.en: The meeting went on for three hours, and nobody could come up with a real solution.

cloze.sentence: 논란이 커지자 구단은 공식 입장을 {{}} 사태 수습에 나섰다.
cloze.en: As the controversy grew, the club issued an official statement and set about damage control.

cloze.sentence: 비판만 하지 말고 대안을 {{}} 봐.
cloze.en: Don't just criticize. Come up with an alternative.

nuance.situation: 전문가 위원회가 문제를 해결할 방법을 제시했다. (An expert committee proposed a way to solve the problem.)

options.why: Putting forward plans, measures or statements is 내놓다.
내리다 goes with decisions, conclusions and orders (결론을 내리다). Proposals are 내놓다 or 제시하다.

items.mnemonic: 건들다 is the accepted short form: 건들지 마.

collocations.en: to mess with other people's things

examples.ko: 내 책상 위 서류는 순서대로 놔둔 거니까 건드리지 마.
examples.en: The papers on my desk are in order, so don't touch them.

examples.ko: 고양이가 자고 있을 때 건드리면 할퀼 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you poke the cat while it's sleeping, it might scratch you.

cloze.sentence: 전시품은 손으로 {{}} 마시고 눈으로만 감상해 주세요.
cloze.en: Please don't touch the exhibits. Look only.

cloze.sentence: 설정을 잘못 {{}} 프로그램이 아예 안 켜진다.
cloze.en: I messed with the settings and now the program won't even start.

examples.ko: 괜히 실직 얘기를 꺼내서 친구 아픈 데를 건드린 것 같아.
examples.en: I think I touched a sore spot by bringing up my friend's job loss for no reason.

examples.ko: 그의 한마디가 동료들의 자존심을 건드렸다.
examples.en: His one remark wounded his colleagues' pride.

cloze.sentence: 그 사람 지금 예민하니까 괜히 {{}} 말고 가만히 있어.
cloze.en: He's touchy right now, so don't go provoking him. Just leave it.

cloze.sentence: 기자의 질문이 감독의 신경을 {{}} 듯했다.
cloze.en: The reporter's question seemed to get on the coach's nerves.

nuance.situation: 농담으로 한 말인데 상대가 몹시 불쾌해했다. 상대의 자부심을 상하게 한 것이다. (A joke offended someone's sense of pride.)

options.why: Hurting someone's pride or touching a nerve is 건드리다.
자존심을 걸다 means to stake one's own pride on something.
자존심을 세우다 means to stand on (or protect) one's pride, the opposite of wounding it.

collocations.en: to look back on the past
to take a hard look at oneself

examples.ko: 한 해를 돌아보니 바쁘기만 했지 남은 게 별로 없네.
examples.en: Looking back on the year, I was busy the whole time but don't have much to show for it.

examples.ko: 남을 탓하기 전에 먼저 자신을 돌아볼 필요가 있다.
examples.en: Before blaming others, you need to take a look at yourself.

cloze.sentence: 누가 부르는 것 같아서 뒤를 {{}} 아무도 없었다.
cloze.en: I thought someone called my name, but when I looked back there was no one there.

cloze.sentence: 이번 실패를 계기로 그동안의 운영 방식을 차분히 {{}} 한다.
cloze.en: We should use this failure as a chance to take a calm look back at how we've been running things.

nuance.situation: 졸업식 날, 지난 4년간의 대학 생활을 떠올리며 생각에 잠겼다. (On graduation day, you thought back over four years of college.)

options.why: Looking back over a stretch of the past is 돌아보다.
둘러보다 means to look around a place (매장을 둘러보다). A stretch of past time is 돌아보다.

collocations.en: to take a walk around the neighborhood

examples.ko: 장관은 태풍 피해 지역을 돌아보며 복구 상황을 점검했다.
examples.en: The minister toured the typhoon-hit areas, checking on recovery progress.

examples.ko: 이사 갈 동네를 미리 한 바퀴 돌아봤는데 생각보다 조용하더라.
examples.en: I took a walk around the neighborhood we're moving to, and it's quieter than I thought.

cloze.sentence: 시장은 취임 첫날 공사 현장 여러 곳을 직접 {{}}.
cloze.en: On her first day in office, the mayor personally toured several construction sites.

cloze.sentence: 경비원은 밤 열 시가 되면 층마다 한 바퀴씩 {{}} 문이 잠겼는지 확인한다.
cloze.en: At ten every night the security guard makes a round of each floor, checking that the doors are locked.

items.mnemonic: 돌아보다 here is 돌아다니며 보다: you move from place to place and check (현장을 돌아보다, 순찰하듯 돌아보다). 둘러보다 is looking around one place or browsing (매장을 둘러보다).

collocations.en: to make fun of the way someone talks

examples.ko: 어릴 때 이름이 특이하다고 친구들이 많이 놀렸어요.
examples.en: When I was little, my friends teased me a lot because my name was unusual.

examples.ko: 남의 발음을 놀리는 건 장난이라도 상처가 될 수 있다.
examples.en: Mocking someone's pronunciation can hurt, even as a joke.

cloze.sentence: 형이 겁쟁이라고 하도 {{}} 울음을 터뜨렸다.
cloze.en: My older brother teased me so much for being a scaredy-cat that I burst into tears.

cloze.sentence: 장난으로 한 말인데, {{}} 것처럼 들렸다면 미안해.
cloze.en: I only meant it as a joke, but I'm sorry if it sounded like I was making fun of you.

nuance.situation: 친구가 넘어진 걸 보고 다른 친구들이 웃으며 장난스럽게 흉내를 냈다. (Friends laughed and mimicked a friend who'd tripped.)

options.why: Making fun of someone is 놀리다.
노리다 means to aim at or watch for (a target, a chance).
놀다 means to play or hang out (with someone).

examples.ko: 주문이 끊겨서 공장 설비 절반을 몇 달째 놀리고 있다.
examples.en: Orders dried up, so half the factory's equipment has been sitting idle for months.

examples.ko: 시골에 놀리는 밭이 있는데 주말농장으로 써 볼까 해.
examples.en: We've got a field sitting unused in the countryside. I'm thinking of using it as a weekend farm.

cloze.sentence: 빈방을 그냥 {{}} 아까우니까 서재로 쓰자.
cloze.en: It's a waste to leave the spare room unused, so let's make it a study.

cloze.sentence: 비싼 장비를 {{}} 두는 대신 다른 팀에 빌려주기로 했다.
cloze.en: Instead of leaving the expensive equipment sitting idle, we decided to lend it to another team.

collocations.en: to bring something up; to start to say something
to take out of a wallet

examples.ko: 헤어지자는 말을 어떻게 꺼내야 할지 며칠째 고민 중이야.
examples.en: I've been agonizing for days over how to bring up breaking up.

examples.ko: 그는 한참 망설이다가 어렵게 이야기를 꺼냈다.
examples.en: After hesitating for a long while, he finally raised the subject.

cloze.sentence: 연봉 얘기를 먼저 {{}} 게 좀 눈치 보여서 가만히 있었어.
cloze.en: I felt awkward bringing up salary first, so I kept quiet.

cloze.sentence: 회의 막바지에 누군가 예산 문제를 {{}} 분위기가 싸해졌다.
cloze.en: Toward the end of the meeting someone raised the budget issue, and the mood went cold.

nuance.situation: 회식 자리에서 결혼 계획 이야기를 처음으로 했다. (At a staff dinner, you brought up your wedding plans for the first time.)

options.why: Bringing up a topic in conversation is 꺼내다.
들추다 is to dig up something hidden or past, usually embarrassing (과거를 들추다).
내리다 goes with decisions and conclusions (결론을 내리다), not topics.

meanings: to let go of (a desire, a burden)

collocations.en: to let go of one's ambitions
to let go; to stop worrying
to step down from a position

examples.ko: 결과는 내가 어쩔 수 없는 거니까 이제 마음을 내려놓기로 했어.
examples.en: The result is out of my hands, so I've decided to stop worrying about it.

examples.ko: 그는 30년간 지켜 온 대표직을 내려놓고 고향으로 돌아갔다.
examples.en: He stepped down from the CEO post he'd held for 30 years and went back to his hometown.

cloze.sentence: 완벽하게 하겠다는 욕심을 {{}} 오히려 일이 잘 풀렸다.
cloze.en: Once I let go of the urge to do it perfectly, things actually went more smoothly.

cloze.sentence: 무거운 장바구니를 현관에 {{}} 한숨 돌렸다.
cloze.en: I set the heavy shopping bags down in the entryway and caught my breath.

nuance.situation: 그동안의 집착을 버리고 편해지기로 했다. (You decided to stop clinging and be at peace.)

options.why: Letting go of something on purpose is 내려놓다.
놓치다 is to miss or lose hold of something by accident (기회를 놓치다).
떨어뜨리다 means to drop something, or to lower a figure (성적을 떨어뜨리다).

collocations.en: to be left off the list

examples.ko: 이번 회식은 사정이 있어서 빠질게요.
examples.en: Something's come up, so I'll sit out this staff dinner.

examples.ko: 최종 명단에서 내 이름이 빠져 있어서 담당자에게 다시 확인했다.
examples.en: My name was missing from the final list, so I double-checked with the person in charge.

cloze.sentence: 교정지를 보니 3장 마지막 문단이 통째로 {{}} 있었다.
cloze.en: Looking at the proofs, I found the last paragraph of chapter 3 was missing entirely.

cloze.sentence: 중요한 회의니까 웬만하면 {{}} 말고 꼭 참석해 주세요.
cloze.en: It's an important meeting, so unless you really can't, please don't skip it.

nuance.situation: 출판사가 실수로 내 글을 목차에 넣지 않았다. (By mistake, your piece was left out of the table of contents.)

options.why: With the piece as subject, being left out is intransitive 빠지다.
빼다 is transitive: someone 뺐다 something (편집자가 내 글을 뺐다).
빠뜨리다 also needs an agent and an object (편집자가 내 글을 빠뜨렸다).

collocations.en: to be caught in a dilemma

examples.ko: 요즘 옛날 드라마에 빠져서 주말마다 정주행하고 있어.
examples.en: I'm hooked on old dramas these days and binge-watch every weekend.

examples.ko: 주력 사업이 흔들리면서 회사는 심각한 경영 위기에 빠졌다.
examples.en: As its core business faltered, the company fell into a serious crisis.

cloze.sentence: 그는 창밖을 바라보며 한동안 깊은 생각에 {{}} 있었다.
cloze.en: He gazed out the window, lost in thought for a while.

cloze.sentence: 어느 쪽을 택해도 손해라 완전히 딜레마에 {{}}.
cloze.en: Whichever way we go, we lose. We're well and truly caught in a dilemma.

nuance.situation: 두 사람은 처음 만난 날부터 서로에게 반했다. (The two were smitten with each other from the day they met.)

options.why: Falling into a state (love, thought, crisis) is N에 빠지다.
A calque of English "fall in love". 떨어지다 means to drop, fail (an exam), or run out.
빠뜨리다 is transitive: to drop or leave something out.

collocations.en: to feel deflated; to lose strength
to go flat; to lose steam

examples.ko: 흰 셔츠에 묻은 커피 얼룩이 아무리 빨아도 안 빠져요.
examples.en: No matter how many times I wash it, the coffee stain on my white shirt won't come out.

examples.ko: 열심히 준비한 발표가 취소됐다니 힘이 쭉 빠지네.
examples.en: The presentation I worked so hard on got cancelled? That really takes the wind out of me.

cloze.sentence: 한 달 동안 야식을 끊었더니 살이 {{}} 바지가 헐렁해졌다.
cloze.en: I cut out late-night snacks for a month and lost so much weight my pants are loose.

cloze.sentence: 범인을 미리 알고 읽는 추리 소설은 김이 {{}} 끝까지 읽기 힘들다.
cloze.en: A mystery novel where you already know the culprit falls flat, and it's hard to read to the end.

examples.ko: 점원 말솜씨에 넘어가서 필요도 없는 물건을 잔뜩 샀어.
examples.en: The clerk's smooth talk got me, and I bought a pile of stuff I didn't need.

examples.ko: 피해자들은 고수익을 보장한다는 말에 넘어가 투자금을 맡겼다.
examples.en: The victims fell for the promise of guaranteed high returns and handed over their money.

cloze.sentence: 그런 뻔한 수법에 {{}} 사람이 아직도 있다니 놀랍다.
cloze.en: It's amazing there are still people who fall for such an obvious scam.

cloze.sentence: 아무리 꼬드겨도 이번에는 안 {{}}.
cloze.en: No matter how you try to sweet-talk me, I'm not falling for it this time.

nuance.situation: 사기꾼의 그럴듯한 말을 믿고 돈을 보냈다. (You believed a con artist and sent money.)

options.why: Being taken in by words or a trick is N에 넘어가다.
넘어지다 means to trip and fall over.
넘기다 is transitive and needs an object (돈을 넘기다). Being taken in is intransitive 넘어가다.

meanings: to move on (to the next item)

collocations.en: to move on to the next item

examples.ko: 이번 실수는 그냥 넘어갈 테니까 다음부터 조심해.
examples.en: I'll let this mistake slide, but be careful from now on.

examples.ko: 시간 관계상 질의응답은 생략하고 다음 순서로 넘어가겠습니다.
examples.en: Given the time, we'll skip the Q&A and move on to the next part of the program.

cloze.sentence: 이 부분은 다들 아는 내용이니까 빨리 {{}}.
cloze.en: Everyone knows this part, so let's move on quickly.

cloze.sentence: 회계 오류를 대충 {{}} 나중에 감사에서 크게 문제가 됐다.
cloze.en: They glossed over the accounting error, and it blew up into a major problem at the audit.

collocations.en: to go past the due date

examples.ko: 번역 원고 마감을 또 넘겨서 편집자한테 면목이 없어요.
examples.en: I missed the deadline for the translation manuscript again, and I can't face my editor.

examples.ko: 회의는 예정 시간을 한 시간이나 넘겨서야 끝났다.
examples.en: The meeting only ended a full hour past its scheduled time.

cloze.sentence: 납부 기한을 {{}} 연체료가 붙는다.
cloze.en: If you go past the payment due date, a late fee is added.

cloze.sentence: 공연은 자정을 {{}} 끝났다.
cloze.en: The concert ran past midnight.

nuance.situation: 약속한 날까지 원고를 보내지 못했다. (You didn't send the manuscript by the agreed date.)

options.why: With the deadline as object, the verb is transitive 넘기다.
With a person as subject, missing a deadline is transitive 넘기다. 넘어가다 makes the deadline the subject (마감이 넘어갔다).

collocations.en: to get past the critical point
to make it through the winter

examples.ko: 의사 말로는 오늘 밤만 잘 넘기면 괜찮을 거래요.
examples.en: The doctor says if he makes it through tonight, he'll be all right.

examples.ko: 팀은 주장의 극적인 동점골로 강등 위기를 넘겼다.
examples.en: The team survived the threat of relegation thanks to the captain's dramatic equalizer.

cloze.sentence: 대출 덕분에 가게는 겨우 고비를 {{}} 숨을 돌렸다.
cloze.en: Thanks to the loan, the shop barely got through the crisis and could breathe again.

cloze.sentence: 화분을 실내에 들여놨더니 겨울을 무사히 {{}}.
cloze.en: I brought the potted plant inside, and it made it through the winter just fine.

nuance.situation: 환자는 수술 후 위험한 순간이 있었지만 결국 회복했다. (After surgery the patient had a dangerous moment but recovered.)

options.why: Getting past a critical point is 고비를 넘기다.
넘어지다 means to trip and fall.
넘치다 means to overflow (물이 넘치다).

examples.ko: 여행 계획을 꼼꼼하게 세우는 편이라 일정표가 분 단위예요.
examples.en: I tend to plan trips meticulously, so my itinerary goes minute by minute.

examples.ko: 교육청은 폭염에 대비해 단축 수업 기준을 새로 세웠다.
examples.en: The education office set new standards for shortened school days in preparation for heat waves.

cloze.sentence: 번역 일정이 빠듯해서 장마다 세부 일정을 따로 {{}} 작업하고 있다.
cloze.en: The translation schedule is tight, so I've drawn up a separate schedule for each chapter and am working to it.

cloze.sentence: 재발 방지 대책을 {{}} 전까지는 공사를 재개할 수 없다.
cloze.en: Construction can't resume until measures to prevent a recurrence are drawn up.

examples.ko: 후배들 앞에서 내 체면을 세워 줘서 고마워.
examples.en: Thanks for helping me save face in front of the juniors.

examples.ko: 그는 끝까지 자존심을 세우다가 결국 좋은 기회를 놓쳤다.
examples.en: He stood on his pride to the very end and ended up missing a good opportunity.

cloze.sentence: 사장은 거래처 앞에서 체면을 {{}} 무리한 약속을 했다.
cloze.en: The boss made an unreasonable promise to save face in front of the client.

cloze.sentence: 그렇게 고집만 {{}} 아무도 안 도와준다.
cloze.en: If you just dig your heels in like that, nobody's going to help you.

nuance.situation: 남에게 숙이고 싶지 않아서 도움 요청을 끝까지 거절했다. (Unwilling to bow to anyone, you refused help to the end.)

options.why: Standing on one's pride is 자존심을 세우다.
자존심을 버리다 means to swallow one's pride, the opposite.
자존심을 건드리다 means to wound someone else's pride.

items.mnemonic: 짚다 (ㅍ) touches a point with a fingertip or cane: 맥을 짚다, 지팡이를 짚다, 문제를 짚다. 집다 (ㅂ) picks something up.

collocations.en: to make a point of addressing (before moving on)
to put one's finger on the crux

examples.ko: 계약서에 애매한 조항이 있으면 서명하기 전에 꼭 짚고 넘어가세요.
examples.en: If there's an ambiguous clause in the contract, be sure to raise it before you sign.

examples.ko: 이 칼럼은 저출생 대책의 허점을 날카롭게 짚었다.
examples.en: This column sharply pinpointed the gaps in the low-birth-rate measures.

cloze.sentence: 지난번 회의에서 나온 문제는 오늘 한 번 더 {{}} 넘어갑시다.
cloze.en: Let's go over the issue from last meeting once more before we move on.

cloze.sentence: 선생님은 내 글의 약점을 정확히 {{}} 주셨다.
cloze.en: My teacher pinpointed exactly the weak spots in my writing.
cloze.cue: point out, put a finger on

nuance.situation: 보고서의 가장 중요한 문제를 정확하게 지적했다. (You pinpointed the report's key problem.)

options.why: Pointing out or putting one's finger on something is 짚다, spelled with ㅍ.
집다 means to pick something up with fingers or tongs. Pointing out is 짚다.

items.mnemonic: Reach → 이르러, 이르렀다 (러-irregular, like 푸르다 → 푸르러). Tell / early → 일러, 일렀다 (르-irregular, like 부르다 → 불러).
meanings: to go so far as to

collocations.en: to go so far as to; to end up

examples.ko: 오랜 논의 끝에 위원회는 만장일치로 같은 결론에 이르렀다.
examples.en: After long deliberation, the committee unanimously reached the same conclusion.

examples.ko: 작은 갈등이 쌓이고 쌓여 결국 소송을 제기하기에 이르렀다.
examples.en: Small conflicts kept piling up until it finally came to a lawsuit.

examples.ko: 창업 초기부터 오늘에 이르기까지 원칙은 하나였어요.
examples.en: From the company's early days up to today, there's been one principle.

cloze.sentence: 산 정상에 {{}} 바다가 보였다.
cloze.en: Only when we reached the summit could we see the sea.

nearMiss.hint: That's the 르-irregular homonym (tell / early). 'Reach' is 러-irregular.

cloze.sentence: 양측은 긴 협상 끝에 합의에 {{}}.
cloze.en: After long negotiations, the two sides came to an agreement.

nearMiss.hint: 일렀다 is the past of the homonym 'tell / early'. 'Reach' is 러-irregular and keeps its stem.

nuance.situation: 토론 끝에 모두가 같은 판단을 내리게 되었다. (After debate, everyone came to the same judgment.)

options.why: Reaching a point or conclusion is 에 이르다, 러-irregular: 이르러, 이르렀다.
이루다 takes an object (꿈을 이루다), not 에.
일렀다 is the past of 이르다 "tell / early" (르-irregular). "Reach" is 이르렀다.

items.mnemonic: A book's 일러두기 (notes to the reader) comes from this verb: 일러 두다, "tell in advance".

examples.ko: 너 또 내 과자 먹으면 엄마한테 이를 거야!
examples.en: If you eat my snacks again, I'm telling Mom!

examples.ko: 할머니는 외출할 때마다 문단속을 잘하라고 누누이 이르셨다.
examples.en: Every time she went out, Grandma told us over and over to lock up properly.

cloze.sentence: 동생이 내가 몰래 게임한 걸 아빠한테 {{}} 버렸다.
cloze.en: My little brother went and told Dad that I'd been sneaking in games.

nearMiss.hint: That form is 'reach' (러-irregular). 'Tell on' is 르-irregular.

cloze.sentence: 그거 선생님한테 {{}} 안 돼, 알았지?
cloze.en: You can't tell the teacher about that, okay?

nuance.situation: 형이 장난친 걸 동생이 엄마에게 고자질했다. (The younger brother tattled to Mom about the older one's prank.)

options.why: Telling on someone is 이르다, 르-irregular: 일러, 일렀다.
이르렀다 is the past of 이르다 "reach" (러-irregular).
들르다 means to drop by somewhere.

collocations.en: too early to say for sure

examples.ko: 결과를 낙관하기엔 아직 이르다는 지적이 나온다.
examples.en: Some point out that it's still too early to be optimistic about the outcome.

examples.ko: 출근하기엔 좀 이른 시간이라 카페에서 기다렸어요.
examples.en: It was a bit early to go into the office, so I waited in a café.

cloze.sentence: 그는 스물셋이라는 {{}} 나이에 첫 소설을 발표했다.
cloze.en: He published his first novel at the early age of twenty-three.

nearMiss.hint: 어린 나이에 is also natural, but the cue is after another word.

cloze.sentence: 아직 포기하기엔 {{}}. 결과 나올 때까지 기다려 보자.
cloze.en: It's too early to give up. Let's wait until the results are out.

nearMiss.hint: That form is 'reach'. The adjective 'early' is 르-irregular.

collocations.en: to make a face; to wear a look

examples.ko: 아이는 칭찬을 듣자 수줍은 미소를 지었다.
examples.en: When she was praised, the child gave a shy smile.

examples.ko: 그렇게 억울한 표정 짓지 마. 네가 먼저 시작했잖아.
examples.en: Don't make that wounded face. You started it.

cloze.sentence: 합격 소식을 들은 그는 어리둥절한 표정을 {{}} 한참 말이 없었다.
cloze.en: On hearing he'd passed, he wore a dazed look and said nothing for a long while.

nearMiss.hint: 짖다 is 'bark'. Facial expressions take a ㅅ-irregular verb.

cloze.sentence: 통장 잔고를 보던 엄마가 깊은 한숨을 {{}}.
cloze.en: Looking at the bank balance, Mom heaved a deep sigh.

items.meaning: because, since (formal written cause: reports, notices, rules, academic prose)
items.nuance: A neutral, logical "because" at home in writing: notices, contracts, reports, papers. In casual talk it sounds stilted; speech uses -(으)니까 or -아/어서. Unlike -아/어서 it takes past tense freely (끝났으므로). Formal notices can follow it with a polite instruction (위험하므로 들어가지 마십시오). ㄹ-stems keep the ㄹ (멀므로), and irregular stems change before 으 (미끄러우므로, 나으므로). Don't confuse it with -(으)ㅁ으로(써), nominalizer + particle, which means "by doing": 노력하므로 = because one tries; 노력함으로써 = by trying. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 103.

contrasts.note: -기에 also gives grounds in writing, but it often frames why the speaker acted or judged a certain way and sounds more narrative; -(으)므로 is the neutral "since/therefore" of reports.
-(으)니만큼 adds "so it is only fitting"; -(으)므로 just states the cause.
-(으)ㅁ으로써 (by doing) looks similar on the page but marks a means, not a reason.

items.meaning: it is/does … (I grant that much), but …: concedes one point with contrastive focus

contrasts.note: -기는커녕 denies the first point ("far from …"); -기는 하다 grants it before adding a "but".
-(으)ㄹ뿐더러 stacks two points pulling the same way; -기는 하다 sets up a point against the first.

items.meaning: whether … or …; no matter (what/who/how) … (the choice makes no difference)
items.nuance: Lists alternatives (A-든지 B-든지, often A-든지 말든지) or pairs with a question word (뭘 하든지, 어디에 가든지) to say the choice doesn't matter; 간에 or 상관없이 can follow for emphasis. Speech often shortens it to -든 (뭘 하든). After nouns: vowel 든지, consonant 이든지. The classic spelling trap: -든지 (choice) vs -던지 (retrospective, as in 얼마나 춥던지 "it was so cold that"). A command or suggestion can follow (가든지 말든지 마음대로 해). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 106.

contrasts.note: -더라도 concedes a single (often hypothetical) fact; -든지 is indifference across alternatives.
N(이)라도 offers one second-best option; N(이)든지 says any of the options will do.
The retrospective -던 family (-던지, -던가) is a different ending; mixing up 든/던 is a common spelling error.

items.meaning: had …; used to … (a past situation that no longer holds, or one set further back in the past)
items.nuance: Korean has no obligatory past perfect. -았/었었- signals discontinuity: the past situation is over or reversed, or it lies further back than another past point. 서울에 살았다 just reports; 서울에 살았었다 implies you don't live there now. With one-off events whose result normally persists, it suggests the result was undone: 결혼했다 (and still married) vs 결혼했었다 (no longer). Translators often overuse it for English "had + past participle". When the English past perfect only marks sequence, plain -았/었다 is usually better Korean. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 108.

contrasts.note: The modifier -았/었던 also points to a closed-off past, but inside a noun phrase (살았던 집).
-곤 했다 means "used to" for repeated episodes; -았/었었다 marks a state or event as over, repeated or not.

items.meaning: it seems …; I guess … (an inference from something the speaker has just noticed)
items.nuance: Draws a conclusion from evidence in front of the speaker: the lights are off, so 다들 자나 봐요. Verbs and 있다/없다 take -나 (or the more formal -는가); adjectives take -(으)ㄴ가 (바쁜가 봐요). 바쁘나 봐요 is very common in casual speech, but the standard form after an adjective is -(으)ㄴ가 보다. With yourself as subject it sounds like discovering something about yourself (제가 요즘 좀 피곤한가 봐요), which is fine but marked. It doesn't state what you already know, and it isn't used for evidence-free predictions; that is -(으)ㄹ 것 같다 or -(으)ㄹ걸요. -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 covers both inference and opinion and is softer. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 109.

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄹ걸요 is a confident guess, often from background knowledge rather than fresh evidence.
-(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 rules a possibility out; -나 보다 leans toward it.
-더라 reports what you actually saw; -나 보다 infers from clues.

items.meaning: (1) at least, even if only (a second-best option); (2) with question words: any … at all; (3) V-아/어서라도: even if it means …-ing
items.nuance: Offers something as an acceptable fallback: 커피라도 마실래요? ("at least some coffee?"), which is softer and more modest than a plain object. Vowel 라도, consonant 이라도. With question words it means "any … at all" (누구라도, 언제라도), close to 누구든지. After a verb, -아/어서라도 shows willingness to go to lengths: 빚을 내서라도. Compare N이나, which can sound offhand or dismissive (커피나 마시자). 지금이라도 is a fixed "even now (better late than never)". See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 111.

contrasts.note: -더라도 concedes a whole clause ("even if …"); N(이)라도 works on a noun or, as -아/어서라도, on the means.
N(이)든지 says any option will do; N(이)라도 offers one modest option.

items.meaning: tends to …; is on the … side; is fairly … (a hedged, relative judgment)
items.nuance: Places a claim on a scale ("rather", "relatively"), which makes it modest. It's typical for describing yourself or your habits. Verbs usually need a degree word or a scale (잘, 많이, 자주, 일찍, 빨리): 많이 먹는 편이다 is natural; 밥을 먹는 편이다 has nothing to measure. For one completed event, V-(으)ㄴ 편이다 rates it (시험을 잘 본 편이다 = did fairly well). For a past habit or state, the tense goes on 이다 (빠지는 편이었다). Rarely used for absolute facts. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 112.

contrasts.note: -곤 하다 describes repeated episodes; -는 편이다 rates a general tendency.
-(으)ㄴ/는 셈이다 sums up what something amounts to; -는 편이다 hedges a trait or tendency.

items.meaning: on the way (to/from) …; (be) on one's way …
items.nuance: Works with movement verbs: 가다, 오다, 나가다, 들어가다, 돌아오다, 내려오다, 출근하다, 퇴근하다. 공부하는 길에 makes no sense. -는 길에 introduces something done en route; -는 길이다 says where you're headed right now (지금 집에 가는 길이야). For an en-route event it stays -는 even in past narration (학교에 오는 길에 만났다). 온 길에 is a different idea ("since I came all this way"), close to -(으)ㄴ 김에. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 113.

contrasts.note: -는 김에 is "while (I'm) at it" with any action; -는 길에 is strictly "en route".

items.meaning: while (I'm) at it; since (I'm) already …, (I'll also) … (using an occasion for a second action)
items.nuance: The first action creates an opportunity, and the second is tacked on because it's convenient. Use -는 김에 when the first action is under way or about to happen, and -(으)ㄴ 김에 when it's done and you're making use of it (부산까지 온 김에). Set phrases: 말이 나온 김에 ("since we're on the subject"), 생각난 김에. The second action is chosen, often a plan, offer, or request (나가는 김에 이것 좀 버려 줄래?); accidents don't fit (넘어졌다). Unlike -는 길에, no movement is needed (청소하는 김에 창문도 닦았다). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 114.

contrasts.note: -는 길에 needs travel; -는 김에 takes any action that opens an opportunity.
-는 바람에 reports an unexpected cause with an unwanted result; -는 김에 is a deliberate add-on.

items.meaning: I should have …; I wish I had … (wistful regret over one's own choice)
items.nuance: Regret about the speaker's own past choice (or "we"), often half muttered to oneself, with falling intonation. -(으)ㄹ걸 is one ending, written attached (할걸 그랬다; 할 걸 is a spacing error here). For negative regret use -지 말걸 (안 -(으)ㄹ걸 also occurs in speech). Politeness goes on 그랬다: 할걸 그랬어요. Plain 할걸요 means something else, a guess ("I bet …"). It is wistful rather than critical. To blame someone, or for a firmer "ought to have", use -았/었어야 했다 / -았/었어야지. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 115.

contrasts.note: -았/었어야 했다 is firmer and can reproach others; -(으)ㄹ걸 그랬다 is wistful and mostly self-directed.
-(으)ㄹ걸요 (rising, conjecture) looks the same in 반말 but means "I bet …".

items.meaning: with … still …; in the state of having … (a resulting state kept during the next action)
items.nuance: The first action is complete and its resulting state carries over while the main action happens, often implying it shouldn't have: 불을 켠 채로 잠들었다. Action verbs take the past modifier -(으)ㄴ (켜는 채로 is wrong); only stative verbs like 모르다 and 있다 take -는 (모르는 채, 살아 있는 채로). It's typical with state-creating verbs (입다, 신다, 쓰다, 켜다, 열다, 앉다, 눕다) and negatives (하지 않은 채). 채 is a dependent noun, so it is spaced (신은 채로). Don't confuse it with the adverb 채 ("not even": 채 1분도 안 돼서) or the suffix -째 ("whole": 껍질째). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 116.

contrasts.note: -아/어 놓다 leaves a result in place on purpose; -(으)ㄴ 채로 describes doing something else while that state lasts.
-(으)ㄴ 김에 uses a finished action as an opportunity; -(으)ㄴ 채로 just keeps its state.

items.meaning: (I saw / found that) …: reports something the speaker witnessed or experienced first-hand
items.nuance: The retrospective -더- reports a past perception as it struck the speaker at the time, so the source must be first-hand (seen, heard, felt, tasted). The 해요체 form is -더라고요; -더라요 is nonstandard. With the speaker's own deliberate actions it is rare (어제 나는 공부하더라 sounds odd), but it is fine for your own feelings or for reactions you observed in yourself (나도 모르게 눈물이 나더라). Past -았/었더라 reports a state already completed when you got there (가 보니 다 팔렸더라). As a question, -더라? is the speaker searching memory (이름이 뭐더라?). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 118.

contrasts.note: -나 보다 infers from clues; -더라 reports what you actually saw.
-던가 asks (often yourself) to recall; -더라 states what you observed.
-더니 links an observation to a following clause; -더라 ends the sentence with it.

items.meaning: was it …? did …? (searching one's memory; also rhetorical "when did I ever …?")
items.nuance: Retrospective -더- plus the question ending -ㄴ가: the speaker searches memory ("Was it Tuesday?"). It is often addressed to oneself; -던가요 checks gently with others. Use -았/었던가 for an event that was already over (우리가 거기 갔던가?). Rhetorically it pushes back: 내가 언제 그런 말을 했던가? (= I never said that). In writing it also makes reflective rhetorical questions (…아니었던가). Spelling trap: -던가 (recall) vs -든가 (choice: 가든가 말든가). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 117.

contrasts.note: -더라 states what you observed (and -더라? also recalls: 뭐더라?); -던가 is a recall question.
-든가/-든지 offer alternatives; -던가 recalls the past.

items.meaning: that (someone) was …-ing / used to …; that was … (retrospective modifier: unfinished, habitual, or closed-off past)
items.nuance: Compare three modifiers on 읽다: 읽은 책 (finished it), 읽던 책 (was reading it, interrupted or still in progress), 읽었던 책 (read it at some point, now recalled as past). For past habits, 자주 가던 식당 and 자주 갔던 식당 are both "the restaurant I used to go to". A one-off past event takes -았/었던 (or -(으)ㄴ), not -던. For adjectives and 이다, -던 and -았/었던 are close; -았/었던 stresses that the state is over. 먹던 밥 is leftover food someone had started. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 117.

contrasts.note: -았/었었다 marks a closed-off past at the end of a sentence; -았/었던 does it inside a noun phrase.
Both carry retrospective -더-: -더라 ends a sentence, -던 modifies a noun.

items.meaning: (I saw that) … and then / but now …: links something the speaker observed to a later change, contrast, or result
items.nuance: The speaker witnessed the first clause, usually about a third person, a thing, or the weather, and connects it to what followed: a change (아침엔 흐리더니 오후엔 갰다), a contrast (어제는 덥더니 오늘은 춥다), or a consequence (열심히 하더니 결국 합격했다). The first-clause subject is normally not the speaker; for the speaker's own action use -았/었더니. Both clauses look back on the past, so the main clause is not a command or suggestion. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 119.

contrasts.note: -았/었더니 is for the speaker's own action and what they then found; -더니 is for what they watched someone or something else do.
-더라 ends the sentence with an observation; -더니 carries it into a following clause.

items.meaning: (when / after) I did …, (I found that / it turned out) …
items.nuance: The first-clause subject is the speaker (or "we"), and the second clause reports what the speaker then found or what happened in response: discovery (문을 열었더니 고양이가 있었다), result (운동을 했더니 살이 빠졌다), or someone's reaction (물어봤더니 모른대요). Close to -아/어 보니까 for discovery, but -아/어 보니까 frames the act as a deliberate try, while -았/었더니 also covers plain results and reactions. The main clause reports; it can't be a command or plan. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 119.

contrasts.note: -더니 reports what you watched someone or something else do; -았/었더니 is your own action.
-아/어 보니(까) is discovery from a deliberate try; -았/었더니 also covers results and reactions.

items.meaning: to think that …!; I can't believe … (surprise, dismay, or admiration at a fact)
items.nuance: Reacts to a fact the speaker finds hard to believe or remarkable. In this use, verbs take the bare stem (그런 짓을 하다니), unlike the quoted -ㄴ/는다니 (한다니 = "to hear that he does …"), which reacts to someone's words. Since surprising news usually reaches us as a report, the two overlap heavily in speech; the bare stem is the form that needs no report behind it. It can end the sentence (벌써 끝나다니!) or be followed by an evaluation (…믿을 수 없다, 대단하다, 말도 안 돼). After 이다 it becomes (이)라니: 그게 다 거짓말이라니. For adjectives the two forms coincide (비싸다니). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 120.

contrasts.note: -ㄴ/는다니 echoes what someone said (그만둔다니요?); bare-stem -다니 reacts to the fact itself (그만두다니!).
-다니까 insists on what you said before; -다니 expresses surprise.

items.meaning: if you keep (doing) …, (eventually) …
items.nuance: Continuing or repeating the first action leads to a natural result or realization. The main clause is a general truth, prediction, or advice (-게 되다, -(으)ㄹ 거예요, -기도 하다, -(으)ㄹ 수 있다, -기 마련이다). One-off acts don't fit (문을 열다 보면). The main clause is rarely a one-time past result; for a result that already happened, use -다 보니. With adjectives it means "when one is (constantly) …" (바쁘다 보면 연락을 못 할 때도 있다). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 121.

contrasts.note: -다 보니 reports a result that already came about; -다 보면 predicts or generalizes.
-기 마련이다 often closes a -다 보면 sentence: the outcome is only natural.

items.nuance: Reports a result or realization that came about by continuing an action (얘기하다 보니 시간이 이렇게 됐네) or from an ongoing circumstance. With adjectives and 이다, it explains a reason rooted in circumstances, softer and more explanatory than -아/어서 (집이 멀다 보니 자주 못 와요; 주말이다 보니 사람이 많네요). The main clause is past or a present state, not a command, suggestion, or plan. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 122.

contrasts.note: -다 보면 predicts or generalizes; -다 보니 reports what has already come about.
-아/어 보니(까) is discovery from one deliberate try; -다 보니 is through repetition or circumstance.

items.meaning: having tried / actually done …, (I found that) …
items.nuance: 보다 here means "try, experience". The first action is a deliberate check or first experience, and the main clause is what the speaker discovered, often contrary to expectations: 막상 해 보니 어렵지 않았다. Words like 막상, 직접, 실제로 often appear. The discoverer is the speaker. Compare -았/었더니 (my action, then a result or reaction, not necessarily a test) and -다 보니 (discovery through repetition over time). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 123.

contrasts.note: -았/었더니 covers results and reactions to anything you did; -아/어 보니 frames the act as a try or check.
-다 보니 = through doing it over and over; -아/어 보니 = after one try.

items.meaning: (1) worth …-ing; (2) good enough to …, bearable, decent; (3) (with 도) understandable that …
items.nuance: Three readings: worth it (가 볼 만한 곳, 주목할 만한 결과), passable or manageable (참을 만하다, 먹을 만해요 = "it's fine, edible" — lukewarm, not high praise), and understandable, usually with 도 (화가 날 만도 하다). It always takes the prospective modifier -(으)ㄹ. Spacing: 볼 만하다 is the base form, and 볼만하다 is also permitted (auxiliary attachment). ㄹ-stems: 들 만하다 (from 들다) vs 들을 만하다 (from 듣다). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 124.

contrasts.note: -는 편이다 hedges a tendency; -(으)ㄹ 만하다 rates something as worth it or acceptable.
-기 마련이다 says something is bound to happen; -(으)ㄹ 만도 하다 says it is understandable.

items.meaning: I told you …; I'm telling you … (insisting on or repeating what one already said)
items.nuance: A contraction of -ㄴ/는다고 하니까, used at the end of a sentence to repeat your own earlier statement with impatience or emphasis ("I said I'm fine!"). It follows the quoted form: verbs -ㄴ/는다니까, adjectives -다니까, 이다 -(이)라니까, commands -(으)라니까, suggestions -자니까. 해요체 adds 요. To superiors it can sound pushy; 글쎄 or 정말 often come with it. Mid-sentence, -ㄴ/는다니까 means "when (I/they) said …" (간다니까 좋아하더라). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 125.

contrasts.note: -다니 voices surprise at a fact; -다니까 insists on what you said.
-ㄴ/는다니(요) echoes someone else's words in surprise; -ㄴ/는다니까(요) repeats your own.

items.meaning: do … (and leave it that way); do … in advance (the result stays in place)
items.nuance: Completes an action and leaves its result in place: 문을 열어 놓다 (and leave it open), 미리 예약해 놓다. Spoken contractions: 놔(요), 놨다. Often interchangeable with -아/어 두다, but 놓다 is the natural choice for leaving a mess or a state behind (어질러 놓다, 켜 놓고 나가다). -아/어 놓고(서) often carries reproach: did X and then (inconsiderately) … (약속해 놓고 안 왔다). For keeping something for later, 두다 is the more usual collocation (알아 두다, 기억해 두다). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 128.

contrasts.note: -아/어 두다 leans toward storing or keeping for later; -아/어 놓다 toward leaving a result in place, including messes.
-(으)ㄴ 채로 describes doing something while a state lasts; -아/어 놓다 is putting that state in place.

items.meaning: do … for later; do … and keep it so (storing a result for future use)
items.nuance: Like -아/어 놓다, the result remains, but 두다 leans toward keeping or storing it for later use: 알아 두다, 기억해 두다, 저장해 두다, 보관해 두다, 비워 두다, 아껴 두다. Contractions: 둬(요), 뒀다 (from 두어, 두었다). In formal writing, 밝혀 두다 / 말해 두다 put something on record. The reproachful "did X and then …" sense is more typical of -아/어 놓고. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 128.

contrasts.note: -아/어 놓다 stresses leaving the result in place (even a mess); -아/어 두다 stresses keeping it for later.
-아/어 버리다 adds finality or relief or regret; -아/어 두다 keeps something for later use.

items.nuance: One ending, written attached: 볼수록 (볼 수록 is a spacing error). Doubling with -(으)면 adds emphasis (생각하면 생각할수록). 갈수록 alone = "as time goes on, increasingly". No tense goes before -(으)ㄹ수록; past time is marked on the main clause (살수록 …그리워졌다). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 132.

contrasts.note: -다 보면 says continuing leads to an outcome; -(으)ㄹ수록 says two things rise or fall together.

items.meaning: only if …; (you) have to … for … (a necessary condition); sentence-final -아/어야지: I must / you should
items.nuance: Marks the first clause as the indispensable condition: 밥을 먹어야 힘이 나지. 만 strengthens it (-아/어야만). With -아/어 봐야 + a negative judgment it means "no matter how much …, it's no use" (말해 봐야 소용없다). Sentence-final -아/어야지 expresses resolve (I must …) or a mild "you should" to others. Unlike -(으)면, which states a plain (sufficient) condition, -아/어야 makes the condition necessary. A command rarely follows -아/어야 directly. After a consonant, 이다 keeps 이 (회원이어야); after a vowel, 여야 (or the uncontracted 이어야). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 137.

contrasts.note: -았/었어야 했다 applies the necessary condition to the past: it should have happened but didn't.

items.meaning: should have …; ought to have … (but didn't)
items.nuance: Counterfactual obligation: the needed action didn't happen. It works as self-criticism (내가 더 일찍 말했어야 했어) or as reproach (네가 먼저 연락했어야지). It is firmer than the wistful -(으)ㄹ걸 그랬다. The negative is -지 말았어야 했다 (안 -았/었어야 했다 also occurs in speech). Watch the tense placement: -아/어야 했다 primarily means "had to" (일찍 가야 했다 = I had to leave early). With -는데 it can also hint the obligation went unmet, but -았/었어야 했다 makes the counterfactual explicit. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 138.

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄹ걸 그랬다 is wistful and self-directed; -았/었어야 했다 is firmer and can blame others.
-아/어야 states a necessary condition; -았/었어야 했다 says it should have been met and wasn't.
-았/었어도 됐다 = "could have" (an open option); -았/었어야 했다 = "should have".

items.nuance: Counterfactual permission: looking back, an option was open that the speaker didn't take (좀 더 쉬었어도 됐는데). Negated, it says the effort was unnecessary: 이렇게까지 안 했어도 됐는데 ("you didn't have to"), a common gracious response to a gift or favor. -는데 or -(으)ㄹ 텐데 often follows to add regret or politeness. Present permission is -아/어도 되다; -아/어도 됐다 can simply mean "was allowed to (then)". See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 139.

contrasts.note: -았/었어야 했다 = "should have" (an obligation missed); -았/었어도 됐다 = "could have" (an option not taken).

items.nuance: Marks a means, tool, or method (= 을/를 가지고, 수단으로). After a verb, nominalize with -(으)ㅁ and add 으로써: 운동함으로써, 줄임으로써. ㄹ-stems keep the ㄹ inside ㄻ: 만들다 → 만듦으로써 (만듬 is a common misspelling). It also marks a cut-off point in time or count: 오늘로써 10년째, 이번으로써 세 번째. It is formal and written; speech prefers plain (으)로 (대화로 풀자). Don't confuse -(으)ㅁ으로써 (by doing) with causal -(으)므로 (because). contrasts.note: (으)로서 marks a role or capacity; (으)로써 marks a means.

items.meaning: you're saying …?! / to hear that …, … (reacting to something just said or heard)
items.nuance: A contraction of the quoted -ㄴ/는다고 하다니: the speaker echoes another person's words with surprise, indignation, or disbelief (지금 와서 그만둔다니요?). The form follows the original sentence type: statement -ㄴ/는다니, question -(느)냐니, command -(으)라니, suggestion -자니. As a connective it means "since (I hear) …" plus a reaction (네가 온다니 기쁘다). Contrast the bare-stem -다니 (그만두다니!), which reacts to a fact rather than to someone's words; for adjectives the two coincide (비싸다니). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 142.

contrasts.note: Bare-stem -다니 reacts to the fact itself; -ㄴ/는다니 reacts to what someone said.
-ㄴ/는다니까 repeats your own words with insistence; -ㄴ/는다니 echoes someone else's.

items.meaning: I bet …; probably … (a guess, often gently correcting the listener)
items.nuance: A fairly confident guess, frequently one that runs against what the listener seems to assume: 지금 가도 문 닫았을걸요. The intonation rises at the end. It is light and conversational, rare in writing, and written attached (갈걸요). In 반말 it looks like the regret ending (할걸), so intonation and context separate them: regret is about the speaker's own past choice and falls; conjecture rises. It is not used to state facts you know. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 143.

contrasts.note: Regret -(으)ㄹ걸 (그랬다) looks back at your own choice; conjecture -(으)ㄹ걸요 guesses about the world.
-나 보다 infers from fresh evidence; -(으)ㄹ걸요 guesses, often from background knowledge.
-(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 denies a possibility; -(으)ㄹ걸요 leans toward it.

items.meaning: (1) …, what can you do / I'll just … (shrugging acceptance); (2) -았/었지 뭐예요: …, can you believe it (reporting a small mishap or surprise)
items.nuance: Two uses, split by tense. Present -지 뭐 (polite -죠 뭐): shrugging acceptance of a less-than-ideal option (택시가 없으면 걷지 뭐; 할 수 없지 뭐). Past -았/었지 뭐예요 (반말 뭐야): telling a small surprising or awkward story, often self-deprecating (지갑을 두고 왔지 뭐예요). The polite narrative form is -지 뭐예요, not -지 뭐요. It is purely spoken, often introduced by 글쎄. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 144.

contrasts.note: -고 말았다 states an unwanted outcome; -았/었지 뭐예요 tells it as a wry anecdote.
-아/어 버렸다 marks finality or regret; -지 뭐예요 adds the storyteller's "can you believe it".

items.meaning: (the thing called) …, as for …: holds up a concept to define it or generalize; also = N(이)라는
items.nuance: A contraction of (이)라고 하는 것은: it holds a concept at arm's length in order to define it or make a sweeping statement (인생이란 원래 그런 거야). The main clause is typically a definition or generalization (…이다, …는 법이다, … 것이다). Before another noun, 란 contracts (이)라는 (김민수란 사람, 자유란 말). The idiom N이란 N은 다 means every single N (가게란 가게는 다 문을 닫았다). Its tone is reflective; it is common in essays and aphorisms. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 145.

contrasts.note: -는 법이다 is a typical main clause after N(이)란: a definition followed by "that's how it goes".

items.meaning: because (I was busy) …-ing, (I couldn't / it cost …): an ongoing activity that used up time or attention
items.nuance: The first clause is an activity that took time or attention; the main clause is what suffered (couldn't do something, was late or tired, spent money) or the effort itself in 수고하다/고생하다 (오시느라 고생 많으셨어요). Both clauses share the subject. Verbs only, with no tense before it (했느라고 is wrong). The main clause can't be a command or suggestion. Compare -는 바람에 (a sudden event, often with a different subject) and -(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 (blame). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 146.

contrasts.note: -는 바람에 = a sudden, often external event; -느라고 = your own ongoing activity ate up the time.
-(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 assigns blame; -느라고 just explains what kept you busy.
-는 통에 blames a chaotic scene around you; -느라고 is your own occupation.
