items.meaning: used to …; would (often) … (a repeated habit, usually in the past)
items.nuance: Describes something that happened repeatedly or from time to time, not constantly: 주말이면 바닷가를 걷곤 했다. It's mostly past (-곤 했다), with a nostalgic or narrative tone; present -곤 해요 = "I sometimes/often …". Verbs only, with the tense on 하다 (갔곤 했다 is wrong). 곤 is the contraction of 고는 and is written attached to the stem (가곤). It is odd with states or one-time events. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 148.

contrasts.note: -는 편이다 rates a general tendency; -곤 하다 recalls recurring episodes.
자주 가던 곳 (modifier) and 자주 가곤 했다 (predicate) both express past habit.
-았/었었다 marks a past that no longer holds, repeated or not; -곤 했다 specifically means repeated.

examples.ko: 입사 1년 만에 영업에서 두각을 드러냈대요.
examples.en: They say she made a name for herself in sales within a year of joining.

production.promptEn: standing out from the crowd (to 'show' it)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean; literally 'a head and horns above the rest'

cloze.sentence: 그 감독은 데뷔작부터 {{}}을 나타내기 시작했다.
cloze.en: The director began to stand out from her very first film.

collocations.en: to have all the bases covered

examples.ko: 그 선수는 공격과 수비를 두루 잘해요.
examples.en: That player is good at both offense and defense.

examples.ko: 이 단어는 구어와 문어에 두루 쓰인다.
examples.en: This word is widely used in both speech and writing.

production.promptEn: widely, all around (across the board)
production.contextHint: native adverb

cloze.sentence: 그는 실력과 인성을 {{}} 갖춘 지도자로 평가받는다.
cloze.en: He is regarded as a leader who has both skill and character.

nearMiss.hint: 고루 (evenly) also fits, but the cue is after another word.

meanings: (as an adverb) all mixed up, in a jumble

examples.ko: 이사하고 나서 서랍 속이 완전히 뒤죽박죽이에요.
examples.en: Since the move, the drawers are a total jumble.

examples.ko: 기억이 뒤죽박죽 섞여 무엇이 먼저였는지 알 수 없었다.
examples.en: My memories were so jumbled that I could not tell what had happened first.

production.promptEn: a jumble, a mess (everything all mixed up)
production.contextHint: native

cloze.sentence: 갑작스러운 일정 변경으로 계획이 완전히 {{}}이 됐다.
cloze.en: The sudden schedule change turned our plans into a total mess.

nearMiss.hint: 엉망이 되다 also fits, but the cue is after another word.

meanings: looking after, supporting (someone through school or a career)

collocations.en: to devote oneself to supporting someone

examples.ko: 부모님이 제 유학 뒷바라지하느라 고생 많이 하셨어요.
examples.en: My parents went through a lot to support me while I studied abroad.

examples.ko: 그녀는 평생 남편의 연구를 뒷바라지했다.
examples.en: She spent her life supporting her husband's research.

production.promptEn: looking after, supporting (someone through school, a career)
production.contextHint: native noun; also as a verb

cloze.sentence: 어머니는 삼 남매 {{}}에 평생을 바치셨다.
cloze.en: My mother devoted her whole life to raising and supporting her three children.

examples.ko: 밤늦게 친구들이 연락도 없이 들이닥쳐서 당황했어요.
examples.en: My friends barged in late at night without warning, and I was caught off guard.

examples.ko: 새벽에 수사관들이 사무실에 들이닥쳐 서류를 압수했다.
examples.en: Investigators stormed the office at dawn and seized documents.

production.promptEn: to burst in, descend on (unexpectedly)
production.contextHint: native verb

cloze.sentence: 예고도 없이 감사팀이 {{}} 사무실이 발칵 뒤집혔다.
cloze.en: An audit team showed up unannounced, and the office was thrown into an uproar.

items.mnemonic: One word: 들통나다.
meanings: the discovery (of a lie or secret)

examples.ko: 몰래 게임하다가 엄마한테 들통났어요.
examples.en: I was sneaking in some gaming and my mom found out.

examples.ko: 경력을 부풀린 사실이 들통나면서 그는 결국 자리에서 물러났다.
examples.en: When it came out that he had padded his résumé, he finally stepped down.

production.promptEn: being found out (as a verb: 'be exposed')
production.contextHint: native noun; forms one word with the verb 'come out'

cloze.sentence: 그의 거짓말은 사흘 만에 {{}}났다.
cloze.en: His lie was found out within three days.

meanings: having nothing to hide, with a clear conscience

collocations.en: to live with a clear conscience
to have something to be ashamed of

examples.ko: 잘못한 게 없으니까 떳떳하게 말하세요.
examples.en: You didn't do anything wrong, so speak up with your head held high.

examples.ko: 그는 떳떳하지 못한 돈은 단 한 푼도 받지 않았다.
examples.en: He never took a single won he could not account for with a clear conscience.

production.promptEn: having nothing to hide (with a clear conscience)
production.contextHint: native adjective

cloze.sentence: 부끄러운 짓을 하지 않았으니 누구 앞에서도 {{}}.
cloze.en: I haven't done anything shameful, so I can face anyone with my head held high.
cloze.cue: have nothing to hide, clear conscience

meanings: infrequent, few and far between (contact, visits)
having let up for a while

examples.ko: 요즘 왜 이렇게 연락이 뜸해? 무슨 일 있어?
examples.en: Why have I barely heard from you lately? Is something up?

examples.ko: 장마가 끝나자 피서객들의 발길이 다시 뜸해졌다.
examples.en: Once the rainy season ended, vacationers became few and far between again.

accepted: having let up for a while

production.promptEn: infrequent, few and far between (contact, visits)
production.contextHint: native adjective; contact 'becomes' it

cloze.sentence: 졸업하고 나서 친구들과 연락이 점점 {{}}.
cloze.en: After graduation, I heard from my friends less and less.

meanings: (___지 않다) to not shy away from

collocations.en: to not balk at the dirty work
to have no reason to refuse

examples.ko: 공짜로 준다는데 마다할 이유가 없죠.
examples.en: If they're giving it away for free, there's no reason to say no.

examples.ko: 그는 위험한 현장 취재도 마다하지 않는 기자였다.
examples.en: He was a reporter who never shied away from dangerous assignments.

production.promptEn: to turn down (mostly negated: 'not shy away from')
production.contextHint: native verb

cloze.sentence: 그녀는 남들이 꺼리는 야간 근무도 {{}} 않았다.
cloze.en: She never shied away from the night shifts others avoided.

examples.ko: 남녀노소를 막론하고 누구나 즐길 수 있는 축제입니다.
examples.en: It is a festival anyone can enjoy, young or old, male or female.

examples.ko: 이유를 막론하고 폭력은 정당화될 수 없다.
examples.en: Violence cannot be justified, whatever the reason.

production.promptEn: regardless of (as in 'regardless of age or sex')
production.contextHint: written; almost only in its connective form

cloze.sentence: 지위 고하를 {{}} 법은 누구에게나 공평해야 한다.
cloze.en: The law must be equal for everyone, regardless of rank.

meanings: bullheadedness, refusing to listen to reason
(___로) stubbornly, no matter what anyone says

collocations.en: to be impossible to reason with

examples.ko: 환불 안 된다고 해도 손님이 막무가내로 돈을 돌려 달래요.
examples.en: I told him refunds aren't possible, but the customer keeps insisting on his money back.

examples.ko: 아이는 집에 가자는 말에도 막무가내로 버텼다.
examples.en: The child stubbornly refused to budge even when told it was time to go home.

production.promptEn: bullheadedness (as an adverb: stubbornly, no matter what anyone says)
production.contextHint: four-character idiom

cloze.sentence: 아무리 설명해도 그는 {{}}로 자기 말만 했다.
cloze.en: No matter how much I explained, he stubbornly kept repeating his own point.
cloze.cue: stubbornly, no matter what anyone says

items.mnemonic: 결재 is sign-off on paperwork: picture the boss as a judge (재판) ruling on your report. For money it's 결제, with the 제 of 경제 (economy).

examples.ko: 팀장님 결재가 나야 비품을 주문할 수 있어요.
examples.en: We can't order supplies until the team leader signs off.

examples.ko: 보고서를 고쳐서 다시 결재를 올렸지만 아직 아무 답이 없다.
examples.en: I revised the report and resubmitted it for approval, but there's still no response.

production.promptEn: approval / sign-off (from a superior, on a document)
production.contextHint: office paperwork, not money

items.mnemonic: 결제 is money: it shares its 제 with 경제 (economy). Sign-off on paperwork is 결재, with the 재 of 재판 (a ruling).

examples.ko: 해외 사이트에서 결제할 때는 수수료가 붙는지 꼭 확인하세요.
examples.en: When you pay on an overseas site, be sure to check whether a fee gets added.

examples.ko: 카드 결제가 자꾸 거절돼서 결국 계좌 이체로 보냈다.
examples.en: My card payment kept getting declined, so I ended up sending it by bank transfer.

production.promptEn: payment (settling a bill)
production.contextHint: money, not paperwork

items.mnemonic: 재량껏 하세요 = 'use your own judgment.' You measure out the right amount (량, as in 분량) yourself.

collocations.en: at one's own discretion, as one sees fit

examples.ko: 회식 참석 여부는 각자 재량에 맡기겠습니다.
examples.en: Whether to come to the staff dinner is up to each of you.

examples.ko: 환불 기준이 애매할 때는 매장 직원이 재량껏 처리해도 된다.
examples.en: When the refund rules are unclear, store staff may handle it as they see fit.

production.promptEn: discretion (latitude to decide as one sees fit)

items.mnemonic: 버무리다 is tossing 나물 with seasoning. 얼버무리다: you toss your words together so loosely that no clear answer comes out.

collocations.en: to dodge a question, answer evasively
to speak evasively, fudge one's words

examples.ko: 언제 갚을 거냐고 묻자 그는 말끝을 흐리며 대답을 얼버무렸다.
examples.en: When asked when he'd pay it back, he trailed off and dodged the question.

examples.ko: 기자들의 질문에 대변인은 "검토 중"이라는 말로 얼버무렸다.
examples.en: The spokesperson brushed off the reporters' questions with a "we're looking into it."

examples.ko: 괜히 얼버무리지 말고 솔직하게 말해 봐.
examples.en: Stop dodging the question and just tell me honestly.

production.promptEn: to answer evasively; to gloss over (a question)
production.contextHint: native word, verb

items.mnemonic: 결렬 has the 렬 of 분열 (split): 협상이 결렬되다, the talks tear apart.

examples.ko: 임금 협상이 끝내 결렬되면서 노조는 다음 주 파업에 들어가기로 했다.
examples.en: With wage talks finally breaking down, the union decided to strike next week.

examples.ko: 양측이 한 발씩만 물러섰어도 결렬까지는 가지 않았을 거예요.
examples.en: If each side had given just a little ground, it wouldn't have come to a breakdown.

production.promptEn: breakdown / collapse (of negotiations or talks)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; news register

items.mnemonic: 결단을 내리다: cut the knot (단, as in 단절 'cutting off') and decide. Don't mix it up with 결딴나다 (ruined): that's what happens when nobody decides.

examples.ko: 회사를 살리려면 대표가 결단을 내려야 할 때다.
examples.en: If the company is going to survive, it's time for the CEO to make the call.

examples.ko: 그 선배는 사람은 좋은데 결단력이 없어서 회의가 늘 길어져.
examples.en: He's a nice guy, but he can't make up his mind, so meetings always drag on.

production.promptEn: a bold decision; resolve (as in making the hard call)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; you 'hand one down' (make the call)

items.mnemonic: 결딴 (hard ㄸ) is a native word for ruin: 살림이 결딴나다. 결단 (soft ㄷ) is a decision. Hard ㄸ, hard landing.

examples.ko: 도박에 손을 댄 지 일 년 만에 집안 살림이 완전히 결딴났다.
examples.en: Within a year of his taking up gambling, the family's finances were completely wrecked.

examples.ko: 그 노트북 떨어뜨리면 진짜 결딴나니까 조심해.
examples.en: Careful: if you drop that laptop, it's done for.

production.promptEn: to be ruined, wrecked, done for
production.contextHint: native verb; sounds like the Sino-Korean word for 'decision'

items.mnemonic: 제재 = 제한 (limit) + 재판 (ruling): a ruling that puts limits on someone. 경제 제재 = economic sanctions.

examples.ko: 정부는 허위 광고를 낸 업체들에 과징금 등 제재를 가하기로 했다.
examples.en: The government decided to impose sanctions, including fines, on companies that ran false ads.

examples.ko: 규정을 어긴 선수에게 어느 정도의 제재가 적절한지를 두고 의견이 갈렸다.
examples.en: Opinions were split over how heavy a penalty was right for the player who broke the rules.

production.promptEn: sanction(s); punitive measures
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; what governments and regulators impose

items.mnemonic: 중재: someone standing in the middle passes judgment (재, as in 재판) between two sides. 중재에 나서다 = to step in as mediator.

collocations.en: to take on the role of mediator

examples.ko: 두 부서의 갈등이 커지자 결국 인사팀이 중재에 나섰다.
examples.en: As the conflict between the two departments grew, HR finally stepped in to mediate.

examples.ko: 형제끼리 싸울 때마다 중재하는 건 늘 막내였어요.
examples.en: Whenever the brothers fought, it was always the youngest who played peacemaker.

production.promptEn: mediation, arbitration (between two disputing sides)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun

items.mnemonic: 묵 is silence (묵묵히, 침묵); 인 is accepting (인정). 묵인 = you know, you say nothing, and you let it stand.

collocations.en: to tacitly allow, turn a blind eye to

examples.ko: 회사가 수년간 초과 근무 기록 조작을 묵인해 온 사실이 드러났다.
examples.en: It came out that the company had for years turned a blind eye to falsified overtime records.

examples.ko: 알면서도 아무 말 안 했으면 그게 묵인이지 뭐야.
examples.en: If you knew and said nothing, that's going along with it, isn't it?

production.promptEn: tacit approval; turning a blind eye (to wrongdoing)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

items.mnemonic: 시인하다 is 인정하다 with a wince: admitting what you'd rather not (잘못을 시인하다). Same sound as 시인 'poet'; the collocation tells you which.

examples.ko: 장관은 초기 대응이 늦었다는 점을 시인하고 공식 사과했다.
examples.en: The minister admitted that the initial response had been slow and issued a formal apology.

examples.ko: 끝까지 부인하던 그도 증거가 나오자 결국 시인할 수밖에 없었다.
examples.en: He denied it to the end, but once the evidence surfaced he had no choice but to admit it.

production.promptEn: to admit, own up to (a fault or an allegation)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean verb; formal, frequent in the news

items.mnemonic: 인지 shares its 인 with 인식 (awareness) and its 지 with 지식 (knowledge): the moment something registers. 인지 능력 = cognitive ability.

examples.ko: 회사 측은 문제가 발생한 지 사흘이 지나서야 이를 인지했다고 밝혔다.
examples.en: The company said it only became aware of the problem three days after it occurred.

examples.ko: 나이가 들어도 인지 능력을 유지하려면 새로운 걸 꾸준히 배우는 게 좋대요.
examples.en: They say that to keep your cognitive abilities as you age, it helps to keep learning new things.

production.promptEn: awareness, cognition (as in becoming aware of a problem)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; psychology and press-release vocabulary

items.mnemonic: 식견 = the 견해 (views) of someone with 지식 (knowledge): you see because you know what you're looking at. 짧은 식견 is a humble formula.

examples.ko: 그분은 미술사에 대한 식견이 깊어서 전시 기획을 맡기기에 딱이다.
examples.en: Her deep insight into art history makes her the ideal person to curate the exhibition.

examples.ko: 제 짧은 식견으로는 이 계획이 다소 성급해 보입니다.
examples.en: In my limited view, this plan looks a bit hasty.

production.promptEn: insight, discernment (judgment informed by knowledge)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; 'my short ~' is a humble formula

items.mnemonic: 면 is face (면접, 대면); 식 is knowing (지식). 일면식도 없다 = 'never so much as seen their face.'

collocations.en: to have never met at all
a perpetrator known to the victim

examples.ko: 일면식도 없는 사람한테서 갑자기 동업 제안이 왔다.
examples.en: Out of the blue I got a partnership offer from someone I'd never even met.

examples.ko: 현관문이 부서지지 않은 점으로 미루어 경찰은 면식범의 소행일 가능성에 무게를 두고 있다.
examples.en: Since the front door wasn't forced, police are leaning toward the theory that the culprit knew the victim.

production.promptEn: acquaintance (having met someone; knowing them by face)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; usually in 'never even met'

items.mnemonic: 식별 = knowing (지식) + telling apart (구별). 식별이 어렵다 = hard to tell apart.

collocations.en: to be hard to make out

examples.ko: 화질이 너무 낮아서 차량 번호판을 식별할 수 없었다.
examples.en: The image quality was too poor to make out the license plate.

examples.ko: 안개가 너무 짙어서 바로 앞차도 식별이 안 될 정도였어요.
examples.en: The fog was so thick you could barely make out the car right in front of you.

production.promptEn: identification; telling apart / making out (visually)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

items.mnemonic: 논란 = an argument (논쟁) that's hard (난, as in 곤란) to settle. 논란이 일다 = a controversy flares up.

examples.ko: 시청이 공원 부지에 주차장을 짓겠다고 발표하자 논란이 일었다.
examples.en: Controversy erupted when City Hall announced it would build a parking lot on the park site.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 과거 발언 때문에 또다시 논란에 휩싸였다.
examples.en: The actor is embroiled in controversy yet again over past remarks.

examples.ko: 그건 논란의 여지가 없는 사실이야.
examples.en: That's an indisputable fact.

production.promptEn: controversy (a public dispute)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun

items.mnemonic: 반론 = 반대 + 논리: an argument pushed back the other way. 반론의 여지 = room for objection.

examples.ko: 발표가 끝나자 한 교수가 표본이 너무 작다며 반론을 제기했다.
examples.en: When the presentation ended, a professor objected that the sample was too small.

examples.ko: 네 말에 반론하려는 건 아닌데, 다른 가능성도 있지 않을까?
examples.en: I'm not trying to argue with you, but couldn't there be another explanation?

production.promptEn: counterargument, rebuttal
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun

items.mnemonic: 논조 = 논리 + 어조 (tone): the key an argument is played in. 비판적인 논조 = a critical tone.

examples.ko: 같은 사건인데도 신문마다 논조가 확연히 달랐다.
examples.en: It was the same incident, yet each paper's slant was strikingly different.

examples.ko: 선거가 가까워지자 그 매체의 논조가 눈에 띄게 누그러졌다.
examples.en: As the election drew near, the outlet's tone noticeably softened.

production.promptEn: the tone or slant of an argument (e.g., of an editorial)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; media analysis

items.mnemonic: 개입 = stepping in (입, as in 입장 'entry') as a go-between (개, as in 소개). 외부 개입 = outside interference.

examples.ko: 중앙은행이 환율 방어를 위해 시장에 개입했다.
examples.en: The central bank intervened in the market to defend the exchange rate.

examples.ko: 남의 부부 싸움에는 괜히 개입하지 않는 게 좋아.
examples.en: Better not to get involved in other couples' fights.

production.promptEn: intervention; getting involved (in another party's affairs)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

items.mnemonic: 개의 is what gets between you and your peace of mind (개 as in 소개, 의 as in 의식). 개의치 않다 = it doesn't get to you. Almost always negated.

collocations.en: to not care what others think
to not mind in the slightest
please don't give it a thought

examples.ko: 그는 남들이 뭐라고 하든 개의치 않고 자기 방식대로 밀고 나갔다.
examples.en: Whatever others said, he paid no heed and pushed ahead his own way.

examples.ko: 답장이 늦어 죄송합니다. — 아닙니다, 개의치 마세요.
examples.en: Sorry for the late reply. — Not at all, please don't give it a thought.

production.promptEn: to not mind; to pay no heed (to)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean 介意 + negation; formal-sounding

items.mnemonic: 경위 uses the 경 of 경도 (longitude) and the 위 of 위도 (latitude): the warp and weft, the whole weave of how it happened. 사건의 경위 = how the incident came about. 경위서 is an incident report.

examples.ko: 경찰은 화재가 발생한 경위를 조사하고 있다.
examples.en: Police are investigating how the fire started.

examples.ko: 지각한 경위를 경위서로 써서 내라고 하더라.
examples.en: They told me to submit a written report explaining how I came to be late.

production.promptEn: the circumstances; how something came about (of an incident)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; add a suffix for 'incident report'

items.mnemonic: 신경 (nerves) + 전 (war, as in 전쟁): exactly what it says.

collocations.en: to wage a war of nerves

examples.ko: 회의 내내 두 팀장은 예산을 두고 보이지 않는 신경전을 벌였다.
examples.en: Throughout the meeting the two team leads waged an unspoken war of nerves over the budget.

examples.ko: 누가 먼저 연락하나 신경전을 벌이다가 결국 한 달 동안 말도 안 했어.
examples.en: We were in a standoff over who'd reach out first and ended up not speaking for a month.

production.promptEn: a war of nerves; tense standoff
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun: nerves + war

items.mnemonic: 구제 shares its 구 with 구조 (rescue): help for people who can't get out alone. 구제 금융 = a bailout.

examples.ko: 정부는 전세 사기 피해자 구제를 위한 특별법을 추진하고 있다.
examples.en: The government is pushing a special law to provide relief to victims of rental deposit fraud.

examples.ko: 외환 위기 때 우리나라는 국제통화기금의 구제 금융을 받았다.
examples.en: During the currency crisis, Korea took a bailout from the IMF.

examples.ko: 방 꼴 좀 봐라. 넌 진짜 구제 불능이다.
examples.en: Look at the state of this room. You're truly hopeless.

production.promptEn: relief / rescue (for victims or the distressed)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; as in 'bailout' (relief financing)

items.mnemonic: 미 means 'not yet' (미정 'undecided', 미완성 'unfinished'): a case not yet closed. (미제 alone can also mean 'American-made'; context decides.)

examples.ko: 장기 미제 사건으로 남아 있던 이십 년 전 강도 살인의 범인이 DNA 재감정으로 붙잡혔다.
examples.en: Renewed DNA testing led to the arrest of the culprit in a twenty-year-old robbery-murder that had remained a cold case.

examples.ko: 그 실종 사건은 끝내 미제로 남았다.
examples.en: That disappearance was never solved.

production.promptEn: an unsolved (criminal) case; a cold case
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun phrase; police and news

items.mnemonic: 구축 = 구조 (structure) + 건축 (building): building systems, networks, and trust rather than houses.

examples.ko: 두 기관은 정보 공유를 위한 협력 체계를 구축하기로 합의했다.
examples.en: The two agencies agreed to set up a framework for sharing information.

examples.ko: 새 팀장은 부임하자마자 팀원들과 신뢰 관계를 구축하는 데 공을 들였다.
examples.en: From day one, the new manager put real effort into building trust with her team.

production.promptEn: building / establishing (a system, network, or relationship)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

items.mnemonic: 허 is empty (허무, 허공): a structure (구조) with nothing inside. It looks solid, but it's made up.

collocations.en: to turn out to be fabricated

examples.ko: 이 소설은 실화를 바탕으로 했지만 인물 대부분은 허구다.
examples.en: The novel is based on a true story, but most of the characters are fictional.

examples.ko: 그가 내세운 화려한 경력은 상당 부분 허구로 드러났다.
examples.en: Much of the glittering résumé he touted turned out to be made up.

production.promptEn: fiction; fabrication (something made up)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun

items.mnemonic: 환산 = 환전 (exchanging money) + 계산 (calculating): doing the math to swap one unit for another. 원화로 환산하면 = converted into won.

collocations.en: to work out as an hourly wage

examples.ko: 연봉을 시급으로 환산해 보니 최저 임금에도 못 미쳤다.
examples.en: When I worked my salary out as an hourly wage, it didn't even reach minimum wage.

examples.ko: 해외 매출은 모두 원화로 환산해서 보고서에 기재해 주세요.
examples.en: Please convert all overseas sales into won before entering them in the report.

production.promptEn: conversion (of currency or units)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

items.mnemonic: 치환 = 배치 (putting in place) + 교환 (swapping): put one thing in another's place.

examples.ko: 수식에서 x를 다른 변수로 치환하면 훨씬 간단해진다.
examples.en: If you substitute another variable for x, the equation gets much simpler.

examples.ko: 그 감독의 영화는 사회 문제를 개인의 감정 문제로 치환해 버린다는 비판을 받는다.
examples.en: That director's films are criticized for recasting social problems as matters of personal feeling.

production.promptEn: substitution (replacing one element with another, in math, code, or analysis)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; technical/academic

items.mnemonic: 지양 has the 지 of 중지 (stop): what you steer clear of. Its look-alike 지향 has the 향 of 방향 (direction): where you're heading. Not 지향 (aim for).

collocations.en: an attitude to steer clear of

examples.ko: 학교는 성적만으로 학생을 평가하는 방식을 지양하겠다고 밝혔다.
examples.en: The school said it would move away from judging students on grades alone.

examples.ko: 회의에서 특정인을 겨냥한 비난은 지양해 주시기 바랍니다.
examples.en: Please refrain from criticism aimed at specific individuals during the meeting.

production.promptEn: avoiding / steering clear of (something undesirable)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb; NOT the near-homophone meaning 'aim for'

items.mnemonic: 지향 has the 향 of 방향 (direction): where you're heading (미래 지향적). Its look-alike 지양 has the 지 of 중지 (stop): what you steer clear of. Not 지양 (avoid).

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 단기 수익보다 지속 가능한 성장을 지향한다.
examples.en: Our company aims for sustainable growth over short-term profit.

examples.ko: 그 정당은 중도를 지향한다고 하지만 실제 정책은 꽤 다르다.
examples.en: The party says it aims for the center, but its actual policies are quite different.

production.promptEn: aiming for; orientation toward (a goal or direction)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb; NOT the near-homophone meaning 'avoid'

examples.ko: 야심 차게 준비한 기획안이었는데 임원들 반응이 영 시큰둥했다.
examples.en: I'd poured a lot into that proposal, but the executives' reaction was distinctly lukewarm.

examples.ko: 선물을 줬더니 "응, 고마워" 하고 시큰둥하게 말하더라.
examples.en: I gave her the present and she just went "Yeah, thanks" with zero enthusiasm.

production.promptEn: unenthusiastic, lukewarm (of a reaction)
production.contextHint: native adjective

items.mnemonic: 넌지시 slides in sideways, like a question asked while looking at something else.

collocations.en: to ask in a roundabout way

examples.ko: 엄마는 결혼 계획이 있냐고 넌지시 물어보셨다.
examples.en: Mom asked, in a roundabout way, whether I had any plans to get married.

examples.ko: 선배가 이번 인사에서 우리 팀에 변화가 있을 거라고 넌지시 귀띔해 줬다.
examples.en: A senior colleague quietly tipped me off that our team would see changes in this round of personnel moves.

production.promptEn: subtly, by way of a hint (asking or suggesting indirectly)
production.contextHint: native adverb

items.mnemonic: 어영부영 drifts like its own sound: no shape, no plan, and suddenly the day is gone.

examples.ko: 주말 내내 어영부영하다 보니 벌써 일요일 밤이네.
examples.en: I frittered the whole weekend away and now it's already Sunday night.

examples.ko: 어영부영 시간만 보내다가는 졸업할 때 후회할 거야.
examples.en: If you just drift along, you'll regret it when you graduate.

production.promptEn: idly, aimlessly (letting time slip by without doing anything properly)
production.contextHint: native mimetic adverb

items.mnemonic: 걷잡다 = gather in and grab hold (걷다 as in 빨래를 걷다). 겉잡다, with ㅌ, means 'estimate by the surface': a different word.

collocations.en: a situation spiraling out of control

examples.ko: 강풍을 타고 불길이 걷잡을 수 없이 번졌다.
examples.en: Fanned by strong winds, the flames spread out of control.

examples.ko: 처음에 바로 해명했어야지. 이제는 소문이 걷잡을 수 없게 됐잖아.
examples.en: You should have explained right away. Now the rumor has gotten completely out of hand.

production.promptEn: uncontrollable; (spreading) out of control
production.contextHint: native; built on a verb that's always negated ('cannot ~')

items.mnemonic: 띠 is a sash: you 띠다 a quality the way you wear a sash (미소를 띠다, 활기를 띠다). 눈에 띄다 is the other word.
meanings: to take on (a color, mood, quality)

collocations.en: to be charged with a mission

examples.ko: 연말이 다가오자 상가 거리가 모처럼 활기를 띠었다.
examples.en: With the year's end approaching, the shopping street came alive for once.

examples.ko: 그는 입가에 옅은 미소를 띤 채 질문을 끝까지 들었다.
examples.en: With a faint smile on his lips, he listened to the question to the end.

production.promptEn: to take on / be tinged with (a color, mood, or quality); to wear (a smile)
production.contextHint: native verb; NOT the near-homophone 'to catch the eye'

items.mnemonic: 곱 double (as in 곱절) + 씹다 chew: chewing it twice, like a cow with its cud.

collocations.en: to turn someone's words over in one's mind

examples.ko: 면접관이 마지막에 한 말을 집에 오는 내내 곱씹었다.
examples.en: All the way home I kept turning over what the interviewer said at the end.

examples.ko: 지난 일을 자꾸 곱씹어 봤자 너만 힘들어.
examples.en: Going over the past again and again only wears you down.

production.promptEn: to mull over / dwell on (words or events) again and again
production.contextHint: native verb; literally 'chew twice'

examples.ko: 반갑게 손을 흔들었는데 다른 사람이어서 머쓱하게 손을 내렸다.
examples.en: I waved happily, but it was someone else, so I sheepishly lowered my hand.

examples.ko: 아무도 내 농담에 안 웃어서 괜히 머쓱해졌어.
examples.en: Nobody laughed at my joke, and I felt kind of silly.

production.promptEn: sheepish, awkward (after being rebuffed or ignored)
production.contextHint: native adjective

meanings: to drag in (a name, the past)

examples.ko: 그는 걸핏하면 회장 이름을 들먹이며 자기 뜻을 밀어붙였다.
examples.en: At every turn he'd invoke the chairman's name to get his way.

examples.ko: 다 지난 일을 왜 자꾸 들먹여?
examples.en: Why do you keep dragging up things that are over and done with?

production.promptEn: to keep bringing up / drag in (a name or the past), usually for leverage
production.contextHint: native verb; disapproving

items.mnemonic: 꾸역꾸역: the sound of cramming in one more bite, one more task, one more step.

collocations.en: to drag oneself to work anyway

examples.ko: 입맛이 하나도 없었지만 약을 먹어야 해서 밥을 꾸역꾸역 밀어 넣었다.
examples.en: I had no appetite, but I had to take my medicine, so I forced the rice down.

examples.ko: 하기 싫어도 꾸역꾸역 하다 보면 어느새 끝나 있더라.
examples.en: Even when you don't feel like it, if you just grind away, it's done before you know it.

production.promptEn: doggedly, forcing oneself on (despite reluctance); stuffing food in
production.contextHint: native mimetic adverb

items.mnemonic: 자못 is 꽤 in a suit and tie: you'll meet it in reviews and essays, not in chat.

examples.ko: 신인 감독의 첫 작품치고는 완성도가 자못 높다.
examples.en: For a debut film, its polish is considerable.

examples.ko: 결과 발표를 앞두고 회의실에는 자못 긴장된 분위기가 감돌았다.
examples.en: Ahead of the announcement, a rather tense mood hung over the conference room.

production.promptEn: quite, considerably (written, slightly literary)
production.contextHint: native adverb; written register

items.mnemonic: 미봉 is darning a hole (봉, as in 봉합 'stitching up'); 책 is a plan (대책). The tear is stitched shut, but the fabric is still rotten. -책 = measure.

collocations.en: to amount to no more than a stopgap

examples.ko: 전문가들은 이번 대책이 집값 불안을 잠시 덮는 미봉책에 불과하다고 지적했다.
examples.en: Experts said the measures were no more than a stopgap papering over jitters about housing prices.

examples.ko: 매번 땜질식 미봉책만 내놓지 말고 시스템 자체를 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: Instead of rolling out patch-job fixes every time, we need to change the system itself.

production.promptEn: a stopgap measure; a band-aid fix
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; ends in the suffix for 'measure'

items.mnemonic: 묘책 = a 묘한 (uncanny, ingenious) 대책: the plan that makes everyone ask, 'Why didn't I think of that?'

collocations.en: to look for a clever fix
to have no clever way out
to come up with a clever plan

examples.ko: 인구 감소를 막을 뾰족한 묘책이 없다는 게 지자체들의 공통된 고민이다.
examples.en: What local governments share is the headache of having no clever fix for population decline.

examples.ko: 마감까지 이틀 남았는데 무슨 묘책이라도 있어?
examples.en: Two days to the deadline. Got any bright ideas?

production.promptEn: a clever solution; an ingenious plan
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; often in 'there's no clever way out'

items.mnemonic: 정쟁 = 정치 turned into 전쟁: politics as a brawl. 정쟁의 도구 = a political football.

collocations.en: to get caught up in partisan fights

examples.ko: 재난 지원 문제까지 정쟁의 도구로 삼아서는 안 된다.
examples.en: Even disaster relief must not be turned into a political football.

examples.ko: 여야가 정쟁에만 몰두하는 사이 민생 법안들은 국회에서 잠자고 있다.
examples.en: While the ruling and opposition parties are busy fighting, bills that affect people's daily lives sit untouched in the National Assembly.

production.promptEn: political strife; partisan wrangling
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; news

items.mnemonic: 정국 = 정치 + 국면 (the state of play, as in a 바둑 대국): where all the political pieces sit right now.

examples.ko: 대통령의 거부권 행사로 정국이 급격히 얼어붙었다.
examples.en: The president's veto sent the political climate into a sudden deep freeze.

examples.ko: 총선을 앞두고 정국이 크게 요동치고 있다.
examples.en: Politics is in turmoil ahead of the general election.

production.promptEn: the political situation / climate (at a given moment)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; news

items.mnemonic: 임대 has the 대 of 대출 (lending): you're the one lending your property out. 임차 has the 차 of 차용 (borrowing): you're the tenant.

examples.ko: 그는 은퇴한 뒤 상가 건물 일 층을 카페에 임대하고 있다.
examples.en: Since retiring, he's been leasing the ground floor of his commercial building to a café.

examples.ko: 청년층을 위한 공공 임대 주택 공급이 수요를 따라가지 못하고 있다.
examples.en: The supply of public rental housing for young people isn't keeping up with demand.

production.promptEn: leasing / renting OUT (the owner's side)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; 貸 = lend

items.mnemonic: 임차 has the 차 of 차용 (borrowing): you rent the place. The landlord's side, lending it out, is 임대 (대, as in 대출).

examples.ko: 회사는 강남의 한 빌딩 두 개 층을 임차해 본사로 쓰고 있다.
examples.en: The company leases two floors of a building in Gangnam for its headquarters.

examples.ko: 계약 기간 중에 집주인이 바뀌어도 임차인의 권리는 보호된다.
examples.en: Even if the property changes hands mid-lease, the tenant's rights are protected.

production.promptEn: leasing / renting FROM someone (the tenant's side)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; 借 = borrow; legal and business register

items.mnemonic: 옹호 has the 호 of 보호 (protect): you wrap your arms around a cause and speak up for it.

examples.ko: 그는 논란이 된 동료의 발언을 끝까지 옹호했다.
examples.en: He defended his colleague's controversial remarks to the end.

examples.ko: 표현의 자유를 옹호한다고 해서 모든 발언을 용인하자는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Defending free speech doesn't mean tolerating every statement.

production.promptEn: defense / advocacy (speaking up for a person, cause, or position)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

items.mnemonic: 옹립: a group props someone up and stands them (립, as in 설립 'set up') on the throne. 후보로 옹립하다 = to rally behind someone as the candidate.

collocations.en: to rally behind someone as candidate
to set someone on the throne

examples.ko: 당내 비주류 의원들은 그를 차기 대표 후보로 옹립하려는 움직임을 보였다.
examples.en: Lawmakers outside the party mainstream moved to rally behind him as the next leadership candidate.

examples.ko: 어린 왕자를 왕으로 옹립한 대신들이 실권을 쥐었다.
examples.en: The ministers who put the young prince on the throne held the real power.

production.promptEn: installing / rallying behind someone as leader (or monarch)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; politics and history

items.mnemonic: 비호 has the 호 of 보호, but the one being protected doesn't deserve it: ~의 비호 아래 = under someone's shady protection.

examples.ko: 검찰은 윗선의 비호가 없었다면 이런 비리가 십 년 넘게 계속될 수 없었을 것으로 보고 있다.
examples.en: Prosecutors believe the corruption couldn't have gone on for over ten years without protection from higher up.

examples.ko: 사장이 조카라고 무조건 비호하니까 다른 직원들 불만이 쌓이지.
examples.en: The boss covers for him no matter what because he's his nephew, so of course the rest of the staff are fed up.

production.promptEn: shielding / protecting someone (often a wrongdoer)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; usually disapproving

items.mnemonic: 의혹 = 의심 (doubt) + 미혹 (bewilderment): something murky enough that people start asking questions.

examples.ko: 한 언론사가 공사 입찰 과정에서 특혜가 있었다는 의혹을 제기했다.
examples.en: A media outlet raised allegations of favoritism in the construction bidding.

examples.ko: 해명을 하면 할수록 의혹만 커지는 것 같아.
examples.en: The more he explains, the more suspicious it looks.

production.promptEn: suspicion / allegation (publicly raised, e.g., of wrongdoing)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; news

items.mnemonic: 회의적 = keeping a 의심 tucked inside. Nothing to do with 회의 'meeting': a 회의적 attitude just doubts.

examples.ko: 전문가 대다수는 그 기술이 오 년 안에 상용화될 수 있을지에 대해 회의적이다.
examples.en: Most experts are skeptical that the technology can be commercialized within five years.

examples.ko: 처음엔 나도 회의적이었는데 막상 써 보니까 꽤 괜찮더라.
examples.en: I was skeptical at first too, but once I actually tried it, it was pretty good.

production.promptEn: skeptical
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean, with the '-ic' suffix

items.mnemonic: 혐의 is the 의심 that hangs over a suspect: 혐의를 받다 (be suspected), 혐의를 벗다 (be cleared).

collocations.en: to be indicted on charges of …

examples.ko: 그는 회삿돈을 빼돌린 혐의로 구속 기소됐다.
examples.en: He was arrested and indicted on charges of embezzling company funds.

examples.ko: 결국 증거 불충분으로 혐의를 벗긴 했지만 이미지는 이미 망가진 뒤였어요.
examples.en: He was eventually cleared for lack of evidence, but by then his image was already ruined.

production.promptEn: charges; suspicion of having committed an offense
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; police and courts

items.mnemonic: 곤혹 = 곤란 + 당혹: boxed in, with no good answer. What you go through is a different word, 곤욕 (곤욕을 치르다).

examples.ko: 기자의 예상치 못한 질문에 대변인은 곤혹스러운 표정을 지었다.
examples.en: Faced with the reporter's unexpected question, the spokesperson looked at a loss.

examples.ko: 둘 다 내 친구라 누구 편을 들기도 곤혹스러워.
examples.en: They're both my friends, so taking sides puts me in a really awkward spot.

production.promptEn: perplexed and uncomfortable; put on the spot
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean root + adjective suffix

items.mnemonic: 현혹: dazzled (현, as in 현기증 'dizziness') and led astray (혹, as in 미혹). Too bright to see straight, so you walk the wrong way.

collocations.en: to be taken in, be dazzled

examples.ko: 고수익을 보장한다는 말에 현혹돼 노후 자금을 날린 사람이 적지 않다.
examples.en: Quite a few people have lost their retirement savings after being lured by promises of guaranteed high returns.

examples.ko: 할인 문구에 현혹되지 말고 원래 가격부터 확인해 봐.
examples.en: Don't be taken in by the sale signs. Check the original price first.

production.promptEn: dazzling / luring into error (being taken in by glitter)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; usually passive ('be dazzled')

items.mnemonic: 오 is 'wrong' (오해, 오류); 인 is recognizing (인식): recognizing, but wrongly. A를 B로 오인하다.

examples.ko: 경찰은 피해자를 용의자로 오인해 체포하는 실수를 저질렀다.
examples.en: Police mistook the victim for the suspect and wrongly arrested him.

examples.ko: 고객이 할인 쿠폰을 결제 수단으로 오인할 수 있으니 문구를 고칩시다.
examples.en: Customers might mistake the discount coupon for a payment method, so let's fix the wording.

production.promptEn: mistaking (A for B); misidentification
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, usually as a verb: 'mistake A for B'

items.mnemonic: 오판 = 오 (wrong, as in 오해) + 판단: a judgment gone wrong.

examples.ko: 경영진이 시장 상황을 오판한 탓에 재고가 산더미처럼 쌓였다.
examples.en: Because management misread the market, inventory piled up sky-high.

examples.ko: 그 경기는 심판의 오판 하나로 승부가 갈렸다.
examples.en: That match was decided by a single bad call from the referee.

production.promptEn: a misjudgment; a bad call
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

items.mnemonic: 착오 = 착각 + 오류: wires crossed somewhere along the way. 시행착오 = trial and error.

examples.ko: 전산 착오로 일부 고객에게 요금이 두 번 청구됐다.
examples.en: Because of a computer error, some customers were billed twice.

examples.ko: 시행착오를 몇 번 겪고 나서야 우리 팀에 맞는 방식을 찾았어요.
examples.en: It took some trial and error before we found a way of working that suits our team.

production.promptEn: an error / slip (esp. clerical or administrative)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; also in 'trial and error'

items.mnemonic: Contracts, licenses, visas: 갱신, a fresh start (think 갱생). Records: 경신, the record changes hands (think 변경). 更 read as 갱.

examples.ko: 집주인이 전세 계약 갱신을 거절하는 바람에 급하게 이사할 집을 구해야 했다.
examples.en: The landlord refused to renew the lease, so I had to find a new place in a hurry.

examples.ko: 운전면허 갱신 기간을 놓쳐서 과태료를 냈어요.
examples.en: I missed the window to renew my driver's license and had to pay a fine.

production.promptEn: renewal (of a contract, license, or visa)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean; the first character has an unusual reading here

items.mnemonic: Records are 경신: the record changes (변경) hands. Contracts, licenses, and visas are 갱신.
meanings: setting a new high or low

collocations.en: to set new records day after day

examples.ko: 올여름 서울의 낮 최고 기온이 연일 기록을 경신하고 있다.
examples.en: Seoul's daytime highs are breaking records day after day this summer.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 자기가 세운 세계 기록을 두 달 만에 다시 경신했다.
examples.en: The athlete broke her own world record again just two months later.

production.promptEn: breaking (a record); setting a new high
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean; same hanja as the word for renewing a contract, read differently

items.mnemonic: 전락 = 전환 (turn) + 추락 (fall): rolling over the edge and landing somewhere worse.

collocations.en: to be reduced to, degenerate into

examples.ko: 수백억 원을 들여 지은 경기장이 대회가 끝나자 애물단지로 전락했다.
examples.en: Built for tens of billions of won, the stadium became a white elephant once the games ended.

examples.ko: 한때 업계 일 위였던 회사가 불과 몇 년 만에 하청 업체로 전락했다.
examples.en: Once the industry leader, the company was reduced to a subcontractor within just a few years.

production.promptEn: a fall / being reduced to (a lower, worse state)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; as a verb, 'sink to (a lower state)'

items.mnemonic: 전가 has the 전 of 전환 (shift): you shift blame or costs onto someone else. 책임을 전가하다.

collocations.en: to pass costs on to consumers

examples.ko: 원자재 가격이 오르자 기업들은 그 부담을 소비자에게 전가했다.
examples.en: When raw-material prices rose, companies passed the burden on to consumers.

examples.ko: 사고가 나자 관계 기관들은 서로 책임을 전가하기에 바빴다.
examples.en: After the accident, the agencies involved were busy pinning the blame on each other.

production.promptEn: shifting (blame, responsibility, or costs) onto others
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; formal, often 'shifting responsibility'

items.mnemonic: 호전 = a 전환 (turn) toward the good (호감, 호평): 증세가 호전되다, the symptoms improve.

collocations.en: to improve, take a turn for the better

examples.ko: 다행히 수술 후 아버지의 상태가 빠르게 호전되고 있다.
examples.en: Fortunately, my father's condition has been improving quickly since the surgery.

examples.ko: 수출이 늘면서 경기가 호전될 거라는 기대가 커지고 있어요.
examples.en: With exports rising, hopes are growing that the economy will pick up.

accepted: take a turn for the better

production.promptEn: improvement; a turn for the better (health, the economy, a situation)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, usually as a passive-like verb ('take a turn for the better')

items.mnemonic: One word, two readings. Read 체, it rhymes with 전체 'the whole': 비용 일체 = all of the costs. Read 절, as in 절단 'cut off', it cuts things off: 일절 금지, always with a negative.

examples.ko: 행사 참가비에는 식비와 교통비 일체가 포함되어 있습니다.
examples.en: The registration fee covers all meals and transportation.

examples.ko: 이사하면서 살림살이 일체를 새로 장만했다.
examples.en: When we moved, we bought all-new household goods.

production.promptEn: all; everything; the whole (of something)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean; 一切 read so that it means 'all of it' (no negative needed)

items.mnemonic: 절 as in 절단 'cut off': 일절 cuts it off completely (일절 금지), always with a negative. Read 체, the same word rhymes with 전체 and means 'all of it' (비용 일체).

examples.ko: 그 배우는 사생활에 관한 질문에는 일절 답하지 않았다.
examples.en: The actor declined to answer any questions whatsoever about her private life.

examples.ko: 회의 중에는 휴대폰 사용을 일절 금합니다.
examples.en: Phone use is strictly prohibited during the meeting.

production.promptEn: (not) at all; absolutely no (with negatives and bans)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean adverb; 一切 read so that it means 'none at all'

items.mnemonic: 유래 = where it comes (래, as in 미래 'what's to come') from (유, as in 이유). Its look-alike 유례 (례, as in 사례 'example') is a precedent. Not 유례 (precedent).

examples.ko: 이 동네 이름은 옛날 이곳에 있던 큰 나루터에서 유래했다고 한다.
examples.en: They say the neighborhood's name comes from a big ferry landing that used to be here.

examples.ko: 명절 음식 하나하나에도 저마다의 유래가 있다.
examples.en: Even each holiday dish has its own origin story.

production.promptEn: origin, derivation (where something comes from)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; as a verb, 'derive from ~'; not the word for precedent

items.mnemonic: 유례 has the 례 of 사례 (example): another example of the same kind. If there's none, it's 유례없다. 유래 (래, as in 미래) is an origin. Not 유래 (origin).

examples.ko: 올해 장마는 기상 관측 이래 유례를 찾아보기 힘들 만큼 길었다.
examples.en: This year's monsoon was so long it's hard to find a parallel since records began.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 유례없는 호황 속에서 직원들에게 특별 보너스를 지급했다.
examples.en: Amid an unprecedented boom, the company paid its staff a special bonus.

production.promptEn: a precedent / parallel (usually as 'unprecedented')
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; NOT the word for 'origin'

items.mnemonic: 띄다 is 뜨이다 squeezed together: something 뜨이다, comes into view, before your eyes. The sash-wearing 띠다 has no ㅢ. Not 띠다 (to take on a quality).

examples.ko: 회색 정장들 사이에서 그녀의 빨간 코트가 단연 눈에 띄었다.
examples.en: Among all the gray suits, her red coat stood out.

examples.ko: 요즘 들어 동네에 빈 가게가 부쩍 눈에 띄어.
examples.en: Lately you notice a lot more empty shops in the neighborhood.

production.promptEn: to catch the eye; to be noticeable (usually with 'eye')
production.contextHint: native verb; NOT the near-homophone 'to take on (a quality)'

items.mnemonic: 데면데면: two people skimming each other's surfaces, never getting past 'hi'.

examples.ko: 같은 부서에서 삼 년을 일했지만 그 사람과는 아직도 데면데면하다.
examples.en: I've worked in the same department as him for three years, but we're still not close.

examples.ko: 사촌들이랑은 어릴 때 이후로 거의 못 봐서 만나도 좀 데면데면해.
examples.en: I've barely seen my cousins since we were kids, so it's a bit stiff when we meet.

production.promptEn: distant, not close (between people who might be)
production.contextHint: native adjective; reduplicated

items.mnemonic: 뜬금 is a 'floating price' with no fixed value: a remark that floats in from nowhere.

examples.ko: 회의 도중에 부장님이 뜬금없이 점심 메뉴 얘기를 꺼내셨다.
examples.en: In the middle of the meeting, the department head suddenly brought up what to have for lunch.

examples.ko: 십 년 만에 연락해서 돈 빌려 달라니, 너무 뜬금없지 않아?
examples.en: Getting in touch after ten years to borrow money? Isn't that totally out of the blue?

production.promptEn: out of the blue; random (and out of place)
production.contextHint: native adjective; very colloquial

items.mnemonic: 에 + 두르다 'wrap around': you wrap your words around the point instead of hitting it.
meanings: to speak in a roundabout way

examples.ko: 그는 제안을 받아들일 수 없다는 뜻을 에둘러 전했다.
examples.en: He conveyed, in a roundabout way, that he couldn't accept the offer.

examples.ko: 에둘러 말하면 못 알아들으니까 그냥 직설적으로 말해 줘.
examples.en: If you hint, I won't get it, so just tell me straight.

production.promptEn: to say something indirectly / in a roundabout way
production.contextHint: native verb

items.mnemonic: 너스레를 떨다: filling the air with chatter so the awkward part slips by unnoticed.

collocations.en: to banter, run one's mouth playfully
to banter with a straight face

examples.ko: 그는 한 시간이나 늦어 놓고도 길이 막힌 게 자기 탓이냐며 너스레를 떨었다.
examples.en: He showed up an hour late and still made light of it, asking if the traffic was his fault.

examples.ko: 너스레 그만 떨고 본론이나 말해.
examples.en: Enough with the banter. Get to the point.

production.promptEn: glib, joking banter (to charm or deflect)
production.contextHint: native noun; you 'shake it out'

items.mnemonic: 볼 cheek + 멘 (볼이 메다, cheeks puffed up in a sulk): the voice that comes out of puffed cheeks. The cheek (볼) is involved.

examples.ko: 주말 근무가 잦아지자 직원들 사이에서 볼멘소리가 나오기 시작했다.
examples.en: As weekend shifts became more frequent, grumbling started among the staff.

examples.ko: 동생은 왜 맨날 자기만 설거지를 하냐고 볼멘소리를 했다.
examples.en: My younger brother grumbled about always being the one stuck with the dishes.

production.promptEn: a sulky complaint; grumbling
production.contextHint: native noun; the cheek is involved

items.mnemonic: 흐지부지: the hiss of a firework that never goes off.

collocations.en: to be swept under the rug

examples.ko: 요란하게 시작한 조사는 책임자 한 명 가려내지 못한 채 흐지부지 끝났다.
examples.en: The investigation that began with such fanfare petered out without identifying a single person responsible.

examples.ko: 운동 계획 세운 거 또 흐지부지됐어?
examples.en: Did your workout plan fizzle out again?

production.promptEn: fizzling out; inconclusively (ending without result)
production.contextHint: native mimetic adverb; often as a verb ('fizzle out')

items.mnemonic: Picture someone fanning embers that were already there: 부추기다 feeds a flame, it doesn't light it.

examples.ko: 자극적인 보도가 오히려 시민들의 불안을 부추겼다.
examples.en: Sensational coverage only stoked public anxiety.

examples.ko: 옆에서 자꾸 부추기니까 나도 모르게 비싼 걸 사 버렸어.
examples.en: Everyone kept egging me on, so before I knew it I'd bought the expensive one.

production.promptEn: to egg on, incite; to stoke (anxiety, spending, a fight)
production.contextHint: native verb

items.mnemonic: 꼬투리 is a bean pod: the critic pries it open, hoping a little seed of fault falls out.

collocations.en: to give someone something to pick at
a slip of the tongue someone seizes on

examples.ko: 그 상사는 보고서 내용보다 맞춤법 하나하나에 꼬투리를 잡는다.
examples.en: That boss nitpicks every little spelling slip instead of engaging with what the report says.

examples.ko: 괜히 꼬투리 잡힐 일 만들지 말고 서류는 꼼꼼히 챙겨.
examples.en: Don't give them anything to pick at. Be thorough with the paperwork.

production.promptEn: a pretext for criticism; something to nitpick (usually 'grab' one)
production.contextHint: native noun; literally a bean pod

items.mnemonic: 마뜩하다 'just right' + 않다: not quite right by the speaker's standards. A contraction of 마뜩하지 않다.

examples.ko: 아버지는 내가 회사를 그만두고 창업한다는 게 영 마뜩잖으신 눈치였다.
examples.en: Dad seemed none too pleased that I was quitting to start my own business.

examples.ko: 그는 마뜩잖은 표정으로 서류를 훑어보더니 한숨을 쉬었다.
examples.en: He skimmed the documents with a look of displeasure and sighed.

production.promptEn: not to one's liking; displeasing (felt as mild disapproval)
production.contextHint: native adjective; written; a contracted negative

examples.ko: 그는 다 알고 있으면서도 짐짓 모르는 척 고개를 갸웃했다.
examples.en: He knew everything, yet he cocked his head as if he had no idea.

examples.ko: 할머니는 손주들 앞에서 짐짓 엄한 목소리를 냈지만 입가에는 웃음이 번져 있었다.
examples.en: Grandma put on a stern voice for the grandkids, but a smile was spreading across her lips.

production.promptEn: deliberately, feigning (putting on a show of something)
production.contextHint: native adverb; written, literary

items.mnemonic: 되레 is 도리어 with the middle swallowed: same reversal, faster delivery. Short form of 도리어.

collocations.en: to bluster when one is in the wrong

examples.ko: 잘못한 쪽이 되레 큰소리를 치니 기가 막힌다.
examples.en: The one who's in the wrong is the one yelling. Unbelievable.

examples.ko: 다이어트한다고 굶었더니 되레 살이 쪘어.
examples.en: I starved myself to lose weight and put it on instead.

production.promptEn: instead; on the contrary (the opposite of what you'd expect)
production.contextHint: native adverb; a short form, common in speech and headlines

items.mnemonic: 미적미적: someone shuffling sideways toward a task they'd rather not face.

collocations.en: to drag one's feet on a decision

examples.ko: 정부가 대책 발표를 미적거리는 사이 피해는 눈덩이처럼 불어났다.
examples.en: While the government dragged its feet on announcing measures, the damage snowballed.

examples.ko: 미적거리지 말고 빨리 신청서 내. 오늘 마감이야.
examples.en: Stop dawdling and get the application in. It's due today.

production.promptEn: to dawdle; drag one's feet (on a decision or task)
production.contextHint: native verb; mimetic stem + the 'keep doing' suffix

examples.ko: 아이를 재우고 난 뒤의 한 시간은 오롯이 나만을 위한 시간이다.
examples.en: The hour after I put the kids to bed is wholly my own.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 원작의 쓸쓸한 정서를 화면에 오롯이 담아냈다.
examples.en: The film captures the novel's lonely mood on screen, whole and undiminished.

production.promptEn: wholly, fully (undivided, all to itself)
production.contextHint: native adverb; slightly literary

items.mnemonic: 현안 = an 안건 (agenda item) left hanging (현, as in 현수막): a matter waiting to be settled.

examples.ko: 두 장관은 이번 회담에서 무역 분쟁 등 양국 간 현안을 폭넓게 논의했다.
examples.en: At the talks the two ministers discussed a wide range of outstanding issues, including the trade dispute.

examples.ko: 오늘은 다른 건 미루고 당장 급한 현안부터 처리합시다.
examples.en: Today let's set everything else aside and deal with the most pressing issues first.

production.promptEn: a pending / outstanding issue (on the agenda)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; meetings and news

items.mnemonic: 현격하다 has the 격 of 격차 (gap): a gap so wide there's no bridging it. 현격한 차이 = a world of difference.

examples.ko: 두 후보의 지지율 격차가 현격하게 벌어졌다.
examples.en: The gap between the two candidates' approval ratings has widened markedly.

examples.ko: 제도를 도입한 뒤로 사고 건수가 현격히 줄었다.
examples.en: The number of accidents has dropped dramatically since the system was introduced.

production.promptEn: vast / marked (of a gap or difference)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean adjective; written; usually 'a marked difference'

items.mnemonic: 현수막 = hung up (현) + drooping (수) + curtain (막, as in 개막 'curtain up'): a cloth hung across the street.

examples.ko: 선거철이 되자 거리 곳곳에 후보들의 현수막이 나붙었다.
examples.en: When election season came, candidates' banners went up all over the streets.

examples.ko: 개업 축하 현수막을 가게 앞에 걸어 놨어요.
examples.en: We hung a congratulatory banner in front of the shop for the opening.

production.promptEn: a (hanging) banner, e.g., for an election or event
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun

items.mnemonic: 거론 = 거수 (raising a hand) + 논의 (discussion): lifting a topic onto the table. 후보로 거론되다 = to be floated as a candidate.

collocations.en: to be floated as a candidate
to be not even worth mentioning

examples.ko: 차기 총리 후보로 서너 명이 거론되고 있다.
examples.en: Three or four people are being floated as candidates for the next prime minister.

examples.ko: 회의에서 그 문제는 아예 거론조차 되지 않았다.
examples.en: The issue wasn't even brought up at the meeting.

production.promptEn: bringing up / mentioning (a topic or a name for discussion)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; often passive ('be floated')

items.mnemonic: 열거 = 나열 (line up) + 거론 (raise): line the items up and raise each one.

examples.ko: 그는 회사의 문제점을 하나하나 열거하며 대표의 사퇴를 요구했다.
examples.en: He listed the company's problems one by one and called for the CEO to resign.

examples.ko: 장점만 열거하지 말고 단점도 같이 써 주세요.
examples.en: Don't just list the advantages. Please include the drawbacks too.

production.promptEn: enumeration; listing items one by one
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

items.mnemonic: 관행 = 습관 (habit) + 행동 (action): what everyone does out of habit, written rule or not.

examples.ko: 명절마다 협력 업체에서 선물을 받던 관행이 올해부터 금지됐다.
examples.en: The longstanding practice of accepting holiday gifts from partner companies was banned this year.

examples.ko: 다들 관행이라고 하지만 그게 옳다는 뜻은 아니잖아.
examples.en: Everyone says it's just how things are done, but that doesn't make it right.

production.promptEn: an established (often unwritten) practice; custom
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; workplace and news

items.mnemonic: 관성 = 습관 (habit) + 성질 (nature): a thing's nature to keep doing what it's already doing.

collocations.en: to keep going out of sheer inertia

examples.ko: 버스가 급정거하자 승객들의 몸이 관성 때문에 앞으로 쏠렸다.
examples.en: When the bus braked hard, inertia threw the passengers forward.

examples.ko: 새 방식이 더 낫다는 걸 알면서도 조직은 관성적으로 예전 방식을 고수했다.
examples.en: Though they knew the new approach was better, the organization clung to the old one out of sheer inertia.

production.promptEn: inertia (in physics, or an organization's habit of doing things the old way)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun

items.mnemonic: 묵살 = 침묵 + 살 (kill, as in 살인): killing a proposal with silence.

examples.ko: 노조의 거듭된 면담 요청은 번번이 묵살됐다.
examples.en: The union's repeated requests for a meeting were ignored every single time.

examples.ko: 회의 때마다 내 의견은 묵살당하는 기분이야.
examples.en: It feels like my opinions get brushed aside at every meeting.

production.promptEn: deliberately ignoring / dismissing (a request or opinion)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; often passive ('be dismissed')

items.mnemonic: 묵과 = 침묵 + 통과: letting it pass in silence. (묵인 goes one step further: silently consenting.) Tacit approval is 묵인.

examples.ko: 이번 사태는 결코 묵과할 수 없는 중대한 위반이다.
examples.en: This is a serious violation that can by no means be overlooked.

examples.ko: 작은 비리라고 묵과하다 보면 결국 조직 전체가 무너진다.
examples.en: Let small misconduct slide, and eventually the whole organization collapses.

production.promptEn: overlooking / letting (wrongdoing) pass unchallenged (usually 'cannot ~')
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; written; not the word for tacit approval

items.mnemonic: 상쇄 has the 상 of 상호 (mutual): two forces wear each other down to zero. Same spelling family as 쇄도; read it 쇄, not 살. 殺 read 쇄 here.

examples.ko: 임금이 올랐지만 물가 상승이 이를 상쇄해 실질 소득은 그대로다.
examples.en: Wages rose, but inflation offset the gain, so real income hasn't changed.

examples.ko: 운동해 놓고 야식 먹으면 다 상쇄되는 거 아니야?
examples.en: If you work out and then have a late-night snack, doesn't it all cancel out?

production.promptEn: offsetting; canceling out
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; the second character has an unusual reading here

items.mnemonic: 쇄도: everything 도착s (arrives) at once, in a crush. 주문이 쇄도하다 = orders pour in. 殺 read 쇄.

examples.ko: 방송에 소개된 뒤로 전국에서 주문이 쇄도하고 있다.
examples.en: Since it was featured on TV, orders have been pouring in from all over the country.

examples.ko: 가격 인상 소식이 알려지자 항의 전화가 쇄도했다.
examples.en: When word of the price hike got out, complaint calls flooded in.

production.promptEn: a flood / rush (of orders, inquiries, or complaints)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, usually as a verb; the first character has an unusual reading

items.mnemonic: 조율 is what a 조율사 (piano tuner) does: getting every instrument, or every party, to the same pitch.

examples.ko: 양측은 막판까지 세부 조건을 조율하느라 진땀을 뺐다.
examples.en: Both sides sweated over the fine print right up to the last minute.

examples.ko: 다음 주 회의 일정은 제가 각 팀과 조율해서 다시 알려 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll coordinate next week's meeting time with each team and get back to you.

production.promptEn: coordinating / fine-tuning (schedules, positions); tuning (an instrument)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

items.mnemonic: 조달 = 조정 (arrange) + 배달 (deliver): arranging for what you need to arrive. 자금 조달 = raising funds.

examples.ko: 스타트업은 이번 투자 유치로 약 오십억 원의 자금을 조달했다.
examples.en: The startup raised about five billion won in this funding round.

examples.ko: 부품 조달이 늦어지면서 생산 일정이 한 달이나 밀렸다.
examples.en: Delays in sourcing parts pushed the production schedule back a whole month.

production.promptEn: procurement; raising (funds) / sourcing (materials)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; business

items.mnemonic: 기조 = 기본 + 어조 (tone): the ground note everything else is played over. 정책 기조 = the basic policy line.

examples.ko: 중앙은행은 당분간 금리 인상 기조를 유지하겠다고 밝혔다.
examples.en: The central bank said it would keep its rate-hiking stance for the time being.

examples.ko: 학회 첫날 기조연설은 노벨상 수상자가 맡았다.
examples.en: A Nobel laureate gave the keynote address on the first day of the conference.

production.promptEn: basic stance / underlying tone (of a policy); keynote
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; economics and policy news

items.mnemonic: 발탁: pulled out (발, as in 발치 'pulling a tooth') of the crowd and lifted up. 주연으로 발탁되다 = to be picked for the lead.

collocations.en: to be cast as the lead

examples.ko: 신인 배우가 오디션 한 번 만에 주연으로 발탁됐다.
examples.en: A newcomer was cast as the lead after a single audition.

examples.ko: 그는 서른 살에 팀장으로 파격 발탁돼 화제가 됐다.
examples.en: His surprise appointment as team leader at thirty made headlines.

production.promptEn: being picked / singled out (for a role, post, or team)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; usually passive ('be picked')

items.mnemonic: 발췌: pulling out (발, as in 발치 'pulling a tooth') the best passages of a text.

examples.ko: 보고서 전문 대신 핵심 내용만 발췌해서 공유해 주세요.
examples.en: Instead of the full report, please share just the key excerpts.

examples.ko: 그 기사는 인터뷰 내용을 앞뒤 맥락 없이 발췌해 오해를 낳았다.
examples.en: The article quoted the interview out of context and caused a misunderstanding.

production.promptEn: excerpting; an excerpt (picking out passages)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

items.mnemonic: 간곡히 부탁드립니다: you bow low (곡, as in 곡선 'curve') in earnest as you ask.

examples.ko: 주최 측은 관람객들에게 쓰레기를 되가져가 달라고 간곡히 당부했다.
examples.en: The organizers earnestly asked visitors to take their trash home with them.

examples.ko: 가족들의 간곡한 만류에도 그는 끝내 사표를 냈다.
examples.en: Despite his family's earnest pleas, he handed in his resignation in the end.

production.promptEn: earnest, imploring (of a request or plea)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean adjective; usually its adverb + a verb of asking

items.mnemonic: 간담회 = a 회의 for frank, friendly 담화 (talk). Not the 간담 of 간담이 서늘하다 ('chilled to the bone'), which is liver and gallbladder. -회 = meeting.

examples.ko: 신임 사장은 취임 첫 주에 직원들과 간담회를 열고 건의 사항을 들었다.
examples.en: In his first week, the new president held a roundtable with staff to hear their suggestions.

examples.ko: 영화 개봉을 앞두고 감독과 배우들이 기자 간담회에 참석했다.
examples.en: Ahead of the film's release, the director and cast attended a press event.

production.promptEn: an informal meeting / roundtable (to talk things over)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; ends in the suffix for 'meeting'

items.mnemonic: 소환 and 소집 share 소, 'call': 소환 summons one person (검찰에 소환되다); 소집 calls everyone together (회의를 소집하다).

examples.ko: 검찰은 다음 주 전 장관을 피의자 신분으로 소환할 예정이다.
examples.en: Prosecutors plan to summon the former minister as a suspect next week.

examples.ko: 그 노래를 들으니까 대학 시절 기억이 소환되는 느낌이야.
examples.en: Hearing that song brings my college days right back.

production.promptEn: a summons; summoning (for questioning)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; legal news, and lately 'bringing back memories'

items.mnemonic: 소집 = 소 'call' + 집합 'gather': calling everyone together. Summoning one particular person is 소환.

examples.ko: 사고 소식이 전해지자 대표는 임원들을 긴급 소집했다.
examples.en: When news of the accident came in, the CEO called an emergency meeting of executives.

examples.ko: 주말에 갑자기 팀 회의를 소집하는 건 좀 너무하지 않아?
examples.en: Isn't it a bit much to suddenly call a team meeting on the weekend?

production.promptEn: convening / calling (people together for a meeting or duty)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

items.mnemonic: 자의적 = 자기 마음대로, by whatever you feel like. Careful: 자의 alone usually means 'of one's own accord' (자의로 그만두다), a different word. Not 自意 (of one's own accord).

examples.ko: 법 조항을 자의적으로 해석해 처벌 범위를 넓혀서는 안 된다.
examples.en: Laws must not be interpreted arbitrarily to widen the scope of punishment.

examples.ko: 평가 기준이 너무 자의적이라 직원들 불만이 많다.
examples.en: The evaluation criteria are so arbitrary that the staff are full of complaints.

production.promptEn: arbitrary (decided by whim rather than rule)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean, with the '-ic' suffix; NOT the homonym 'of one's own accord'

items.mnemonic: 방자하다 has the 방 of 방종 (license): let off the leash, answering to no one. Often in 오만방자하다.

examples.ko: 그는 윗사람 앞에서도 다리를 꼬고 앉는 등 방자한 태도로 빈축을 샀다.
examples.en: He drew disapproval for his insolence, even sitting cross-legged in front of his superiors.

examples.ko: 권력을 잡자마자 오만방자해진 정치인들을 우리는 여러 번 봐 왔다.
examples.en: We've seen plenty of politicians turn arrogant and insolent the moment they gained power.

production.promptEn: insolent, impudent (behaving without restraint toward others)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean adjective; often paired with 'arrogant' in one word

items.mnemonic: 제고 = 높이다 in news-speak: 경쟁력 제고, raising competitiveness. 재고 is either 'think again' or 'stock on hand'; 제고 is the one that raises.

examples.ko: 정부는 중소기업의 경쟁력 제고를 위해 연구 개발 지원을 늘리기로 했다.
examples.en: The government decided to expand R&D support to boost the competitiveness of small and midsize businesses.

examples.ko: 이번 캠페인은 개인 정보 보호에 대한 인식 제고를 목표로 한다.
examples.en: This campaign aims to raise awareness of personal data protection.

production.promptEn: enhancing / raising (competitiveness, awareness, efficiency)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; officialese; NOT the words for 'reconsider' or 'inventory'

items.mnemonic: 혼동 = 혼합 (mixing) + 동일 (same): mixing two things up until they seem the same. 혼돈 is a world without order.

collocations.en: to be easy to mix up

examples.ko: '결재'와 '결제'는 발음이 같아서 혼동하기 쉽다.
examples.en: 결재 and 결제 sound the same, so they're easy to mix up.

examples.ko: 두 회사의 로고가 너무 비슷해서 소비자들에게 혼동을 줄 우려가 있다.
examples.en: The two companies' logos are so alike that consumers may confuse them.

production.promptEn: confusion (mixing up A with B); a mix-up
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; NOT the near-homophone meaning 'chaos'

items.mnemonic: 혼돈 is chaos, the formless soup before creation (혼돈의 시대). 혼동 is mixing up two particular things (A와 B를 혼동하다).

examples.ko: 정권이 무너진 뒤 그 나라는 한동안 깊은 혼돈에 빠졌다.
examples.en: After the regime fell, the country sank into deep chaos for a time.

examples.ko: 이사 첫날 우리 집은 그야말로 혼돈 그 자체였다.
examples.en: On moving day our place was sheer chaos.

production.promptEn: chaos; disorder
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; NOT the near-homophone meaning 'mixing two things up'

items.mnemonic: 녹록: small, ordinary pebbles, easy to step over. Life, it turns out, is 녹록지 않다.
meanings: easy to deal with, a pushover

examples.ko: 청년들이 혼자 힘으로 집을 마련하기란 결코 녹록지 않다.
examples.en: It's no easy matter for young people to get a home on their own.

examples.ko: 상대 팀이 생각보다 녹록지 않네. 긴장 좀 해야겠어.
examples.en: The other team is tougher than I thought. We need to stay sharp.

production.promptEn: easy to handle, a pushover (almost always negated: 'no easy matter')
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean adjective (碌碌)

items.mnemonic: 깜냥: the size of the load you can actually carry, not the one you wish you could.

collocations.en: to not be up to it

examples.ko: 팀장 자리는 솔직히 내 깜냥으로는 감당이 안 될 것 같아.
examples.en: Honestly, I don't think I'm up to being team leader.

examples.ko: 그는 자기 깜냥도 모르고 큰 사업에 덤볐다가 빚만 졌다.
examples.en: Without knowing his own limits, he plunged into a big venture and ended up deep in debt.

production.promptEn: one's capacity / what one can handle (often said modestly)
production.contextHint: native noun; 'with my ~'

items.mnemonic: 지레 jumps the gun: scared, certain, or giving up before anything has happened.

examples.ko: 해 보지도 않고 지레 겁먹을 필요는 없어.
examples.en: There's no need to get scared before you've even tried.

examples.ko: 그는 상대가 거절할 거라고 지레짐작하고 아예 제안을 하지 않았다.
examples.en: Assuming the other side would refuse, he never even made the offer.

production.promptEn: prematurely; in advance (before there's any reason to)
production.contextHint: native adverb; 'get scared prematurely'

items.mnemonic: 고스란히: the cake carried across the room without losing a single crumb.

examples.ko: 할머니가 쓰시던 방은 돌아가신 뒤에도 고스란히 남아 있었다.
examples.en: Grandmother's room stayed untouched even after she passed away.

examples.ko: 원자재 값이 오른 부담은 고스란히 소비자에게 돌아갔다.
examples.en: The entire burden of higher raw-material prices was passed straight on to consumers.

production.promptEn: intact, untouched; (passed on) undiminished
production.contextHint: native adverb

items.mnemonic: 아우르다: an arm around everyone in the photo, every generation in one frame.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 노래는 세대를 아우르는 인기를 누리고 있다.
examples.en: The singer's songs are popular across generations.

examples.ko: 이번 전시는 회화와 사진, 영상을 아우르는 대규모 기획전이다.
examples.en: This is a large-scale exhibition spanning painting, photography, and video.

production.promptEn: to encompass / bring together (groups, genres, or generations)
production.contextHint: native verb

items.mnemonic: 북받치다: something pushing up from deep in the chest until it's caught in your throat.

collocations.en: a wave of hurt wells up

examples.ko: 수상 소감을 말하던 그는 감정이 북받쳐 끝내 말을 잇지 못했다.
examples.en: Giving his acceptance speech, he was overcome with emotion and couldn't go on.

examples.ko: 엄마 목소리를 듣자마자 서러움이 북받쳐서 엉엉 울었어.
examples.en: The moment I heard Mom's voice, all the hurt welled up and I sobbed.

production.promptEn: (of emotion) to well up; to be overcome
production.contextHint: native verb

items.mnemonic: 사그라들다: embers settling into ash, one soft hiss at a time.

examples.ko: 한때 뜨거웠던 투자 열기가 금리 인상과 함께 빠르게 사그라들었다.
examples.en: The once red-hot investment fever quickly died down as interest rates rose.

examples.ko: 화가 좀 사그라들면 그때 다시 얘기하자.
examples.en: Let's talk again once you've cooled down a bit.

production.promptEn: to die down; subside (fire, anger, enthusiasm)
production.contextHint: native verb

items.mnemonic: 얼렁뚱땅: a quick shuffle of the cards so no one looks too closely.
meanings: glossing over (to get away with it)

examples.ko: 실수를 얼렁뚱땅 넘기려다가 오히려 일이 커졌다.
examples.en: He tried to fudge his way past the mistake, and it only blew up.

examples.ko: 숙제를 얼렁뚱땅 해 가면 선생님이 다 알아.
examples.en: If you do your homework any old way, the teacher can tell.

production.promptEn: sloppily, slapdash (fudging something to get it over with or get away with it)
production.contextHint: native mimetic adverb

items.mnemonic: 시답잖다 comes from 실답지 않다: nothing 실 (solid, substantial) about it.

examples.ko: 다들 바쁜데 시답잖은 얘기로 회의 시간을 잡아먹지 맙시다.
examples.en: Everyone's busy, so let's not eat up meeting time with trivial chatter.

examples.ko: 걔는 내 고민을 시답잖다는 듯이 듣더라.
examples.en: He listened to my worries as if they were hardly worth bothering about.

production.promptEn: trivial, not worth bothering with (silly, lame)
production.contextHint: native adjective; colloquial

items.mnemonic: 하물며 raises the stakes: 'if even X…, then how much more Y.'

examples.ko: 전문가도 풀기 어려운 문제인데 하물며 초보자야 오죽하겠는가.
examples.en: It's a hard problem even for experts, let alone for a beginner.

examples.ko: 평소에도 주차할 데가 없는 동넨데, 하물며 명절 연휴야 말할 것도 없지.
examples.en: It's hard to find parking around here on a normal day, let alone over the holidays.

production.promptEn: let alone; much less (all the more so)
production.contextHint: native adverb; written, often closing with a rhetorical question

items.mnemonic: 버젓이: standing up straight in broad daylight, as if nothing were wrong.

examples.ko: 단속이 끝나자 불법 노점들이 다시 버젓이 영업을 시작했다.
examples.en: As soon as the crackdown ended, the illegal street stalls brazenly reopened.

examples.ko: 증거가 다 있는데도 버젓이 거짓말을 하더라.
examples.en: Even with all the evidence there, he lied to my face.

production.promptEn: brazenly, openly (without shame or concealment)
production.contextHint: native adverb

items.mnemonic: 서슴다 = to hesitate; 서슴없이 = with zero hesitation. From 서슴다 'to hesitate'. Nothing in the way (unstoppable) is 거침없이.

examples.ko: 그는 질문을 받자 서슴없이 자신의 실수를 인정했다.
examples.en: When asked, he admitted his mistake without hesitation.

examples.ko: 모르는 게 있으면 서슴없이 물어보세요.
examples.en: If there's anything you don't know, don't hesitate to ask.

production.promptEn: without hesitation; unhesitatingly
production.contextHint: native adverb; from a verb meaning 'to hesitate'. Not 'unstoppable (nothing in the way)'

items.mnemonic: 애먼: the bystander who catches the punch meant for someone else.

collocations.en: to take it out on the wrong person

examples.ko: 근거 없는 소문 때문에 애먼 사람이 피해를 봤다.
examples.en: Because of a baseless rumor, an innocent person got hurt.

examples.ko: 회사에서 깨지고 와서 왜 애먼 나한테 화풀이야?
examples.en: You got chewed out at work, so why take it out on me?

production.promptEn: innocent / the wrong (person): someone who doesn't deserve the blame or harm
production.contextHint: native determiner, before a noun

items.mnemonic: 들추다: lifting the lid to see what's hidden underneath. Often 들춰내다.

collocations.en: to dig up, bring to light

examples.ko: 청문회에서 야당 의원들은 후보자의 오래된 비리를 하나하나 들춰냈다.
examples.en: At the hearing, opposition lawmakers dug up the nominee's old misdeeds one by one.

examples.ko: 이미 끝난 얘기를 왜 자꾸 들추는 거야?
examples.en: Why do you keep raking up something that's already settled?

production.promptEn: to dig up / rake up (past faults or secrets); to rummage through
production.contextHint: native verb; often compounded with 'take out'

items.mnemonic: 떠 (lift off) + 넘기다 (hand over): lift the load off your own back and over onto someone else's. Everyday counterpart of 전가하다.
meanings: to dump (a task or blame) on

collocations.en: to pass the buck back and forth

examples.ko: 팀장은 자기가 저지른 실수를 막내에게 떠넘겼다.
examples.en: The team lead pinned his own mistake on the most junior member.

examples.ko: 하기 싫은 일을 나한테 떠넘기지 마.
examples.en: Don't dump the jobs you don't want on me.

production.promptEn: to foist / dump (a task, blame, or burden) onto someone else
production.contextHint: native verb; everyday counterpart of the formal word for 'shift (blame)'
